items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: require DELETE access for delete-on-close opens smb2_open() accepts FILE_DELETE_ON_CLOSE on an existing file without DELETE in DesiredAccess. When the request asks only for FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES or READ_CONTROL, it also skips inode_permission() and the parent directory MAY_WRITE | MAY_EXEC check that delete-on-close is meant to get. The file is then marked for deletion by a caller who could not delete it. The unlink happens later, in __ksmbd_inode_close(), when the last handle on the inode is closed, and it runs with the credentials of that handle. If the caller closes last, the unlink fails. If another user who can write the parent directory, such as the file's owner, still has the file open, the file is deleted when that user closes it. Until then new opens of the file fail with STATUS_DELETE_PENDING. So a user with only search permission on a directory can delete a file in it, or block opens of it, while the owner has it open. A MAXIMUM_ALLOWED open that also requests DELETE has the same problem. The requested access is replaced with the maximal access, which does not include DELETE when the caller cannot

items.title: CVE-2026-99736: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: fix accounting of swapin-error markers A failed swap read replaces the swap entry with a swapin-erro
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: fix accounting of swapin-error markers A failed swap read replaces the swap entry with a swapin-error marker in the page-cache and subtracts its pages from "alloced" and "swapped"; however, it leaves their block charge in place. Removing the marker during truncate then subtracts from "swapped" again. This can underflow the counters or make swapped reach zero while other pages remain swapped out, causing swapoff to loop without finding them. When installing the marker, subtract only from "swapped" and let shmem_recalc_inode() reduce "alloced" and release the block charge. Make shmem_free_swap() report successful removal separately from the number of swap pages freed, so removing a swapin-error marker does not subtract from "swapped" again. It's a bit confusing, but replacing a swapped out page by a swapin-error marker in shmem_set_folio_swapin_error() behaves as follows: Initially: alloced=1, swapped=1, nrpages=0 Calling shmem_recalc_inode(inode, 0, -1) -> swapped = 0 -> freed = 1 - 0 - 0 = 1 -> alloced -= freed -> alloced=0, swapped=0, block charge released

items.title: CVE-2026-99737: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: fix truncate loop after boundary swapin failure If swapping in a large entry at the new EOF fails, s
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: fix truncate loop after boundary swapin failure If swapping in a large entry at the new EOF fails, shmem_undo_range() leaves the entry in place. Its final scan skips the entry, then restarts from the same start index and finds it again. Truncation can loop forever while holding i_rwsem. Advance start past the skipped entry so that a restarted scan can finish, as we already do for folios that cannot be split. Note that this does not fix the missing zeroing when boundary swapin fails, it merely prevents the endless loop.

items.title: CVE-2026-99738: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: preserve allocation errors when swapping in large entries shmem_swapin_folio() adjusts swap to the r
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: preserve allocation errors when swapping in large entries shmem_swapin_folio() adjusts swap to the requested slot within a large swap entry before allocating a folio. If allocation or charging fails, the error path compares this adjusted value with the original entry still stored in the XArray in shmem_confirm_swap(). Unless the index is at the start of the entry, this turns -ENOMEM into -EEXIST even though nothing changed. The caller retries -EEXIST, so persistent allocation failures can leave the task spinning instead of returning the error. Restore swap to index_entry on allocation failure so the existing error path checks the original entry. This preserves the allocation error if the entry is unchanged and still retries if it changed concurrently.

items.title: CVE-2026-99739: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: fix truncate hang in large swap entry Truncating a tmpfs file or memfd to a page-aligned size inside
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: fix truncate hang in large swap entry Truncating a tmpfs file or memfd to a page-aligned size inside a large swap entry can loop indefinitely in shmem_undo_range(). The task holds the inode lock and cannot be killed. A large swap entry represents a whole swapped-out folio. For example, truncate a file whose pages 0-7 share one swap entry to four pages: [ 0 1 2 3 | 4 5 6 7 ] keep | discard ^ new EOF, start = 4 i_size has already been updated when boundary handling asks shmem_get_partial_folio() for page 4. Since it is swapped out, the helper calls shmem_get_folio() with SGP_READ. That rejects page 4 with -EINVAL because its starting offset equals i_size. Nothing is read back. The final scan cannot free the entry without losing pages 0-3. It skips it, restarts from start = 4, and finds it again indefinitely. An unaligned truncate avoids this particular failure because the requested page starts below i_size. Folios already in the page-cache cannot trigger it as the direct lookup will return them beyond EOF. Fix it by letting shmem_get_partial_folio() call shmem_swapin_folio() directly for swap entries. items.title: CVE-2026-99740: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split A fault or collapse can insert a large folio crossing EOF
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split A fault or collapse can insert a large folio crossing EOF after shmem_undo_range() has handled the boundary folios. If splitting that folio fails, truncate_inode_partial_folio() retains it when it is dirty. The final scan then repeatedly finds it because it restarts from an unchanged start. Truncation keeps the inode lock and ignores fatal signals while looping. A concurrent unlink() can then block other directory operations while holding the directory lock and waiting for the file's lock. Advance start past the retained folio, whose truncated part has already been zeroed. Do not move start backwards if the failed split has shrunk the folio. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: split fixes, simplify descriptions, adjust comments ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99741: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: tmpfs: keep the quota soft limits of an unused id When the last reference to a dquot goes away, shmem_release_
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: tmpfs: keep the quota soft limits of an unused id When the last reference to a dquot goes away, shmem_release_dquot() stores its limits in the rb tree of the mount, unless shmem_is_empty_dquot() says that there is nothing worth storing. That function looks at the usage and at the two hard limits only. So if the administrator sets nothing but soft limits for an id that owns no file yet, the entry is thrown away as soon as the dquot that Q_SETQUOTA used is released, and the id never gets to see a limit. To fix it, compare the soft limits as well: an entry can be empty only if both soft limits are zero as well, which is exactly what shmem_acquire_dquot() sets for a new entry. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: slightly adjusted description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99742: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mempolicy: charge shared policy nodes Any local user can bypass memory.max with mbind() on a tmpfs file, an
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mempolicy: charge shared policy nodes Any local user can bypass memory.max with mbind() on a tmpfs file, and allocate unbounded kernel memory. mbind() sets a NUMA memory policy for a range of a mapping. If the mapping is of a shmem and friends, the kernel also stores the policy on the inode, in a tree with one entry per range of the file. Each mbind() on a single page of a mapping can add one shared policy node (struct sp_node) and one struct mempolicy to that tree. They outlive the mapping and stay around until the inode is destroyed. The tree is not bounded by the file size, so the file can be empty. Memory that user space can allocate must be charged to a memory cgroup. A slab cache does that for all of its objects if it is created with SLAB_ACCOUNT. numa_policy_init() creates the slab caches for both structs without SLAB_ACCOUNT, so they are not charged to any cgroup. Reproduced with mbind() on single pages of an empty tmpfs file, from a cgroup with memory.max=8M: the global OOM killer killed tasks owned by root, and the machine panicked. Fix this by creating both caches with SLAB_ACCOUNT. This change implie

items.title: CVE-2026-99729: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/rmap: handle device-exclusive entries in folio_referenced_one() page_vma_mapped_walk() can return non-prese
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/rmap: handle device-exclusive entries in folio_referenced_one() page_vma_mapped_walk() can return non-present device-exclusive entries, but folio_referenced_one() passes them to PTE young-bit accessors that require present PTEs. We must neither call clear_flush_young_ptes_notify() nor folio_pte_batch() with non-present entries. For example, clearing the young bit on non-present PTEs can corrupt the entry: on arm64 PTE_AF overlaps the swap type, so clearing it turns a device-exclusive entry into an ordinary swap entry. folio_pte_batch() will VM_WARN_ON_FOLIO. Apply the same approach as the previous fixes to e.g., damon_ptep_mkold(): treat these entries as old from the CPU's perspective and obtain their young state through the MMU notifier. Skip PTE batching and MGLRU look-around for non-present entries, and don't modify non-present PTEs.

items.title: CVE-2026-99730: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/filemap: finish fault cleanup before dropping the fault lock On a retried fault, a fatal signal interruptin
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/filemap: finish fault cleanup before dropping the fault lock On a retried fault, a fatal signal interrupting the folio lock wait makes lock_folio_maybe_drop_mmap() drop the fault lock without pinning the file. However, filemap_fault() may still need to release mapping->invalidate_lock. A concurrent munmap() can release the last file reference and free the mapping before that unlock. Defer dropping the fault lock to filemap_fault()'s retry cleanup, after releasing invalidate_lock. If the fault lock was already dropped for I/O, release the existing file reference instead. Keep the fault lock held for FAULT_FLAG_RETRY_NOWAIT as before.

items.title: CVE-2026-99731: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/filemap: don't lose a folio lock wakeup to a signal An exclusive waiter in folio_wait_bit_common() can leav
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/filemap: don't lose a folio lock wakeup to a signal An exclusive waiter in folio_wait_bit_common() can leave the wait loop because of a fatal signal, then be woken by folio_unlock() before finish_wait(). If the waker did not hand over the lock, the waiter returns -EINTR without trying to acquire it. folio_wake_bit() stops after waking the first exclusive waiter, so this loses the wakeup and can leave other waiters asleep indefinitely on an unlocked folio. After finish_wait(), let a waiter woken without a lock handoff try once more to acquire the lock. If successful, return success so the caller's eventual unlock wakes the next waiter. Otherwise, the current lock owner will do so. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: clarify and simplify comment + description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99732: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/filemap: read mapping->a_ops->free_folio under i_lock memory_failure() -> ... -> filemap_remove_folio() can
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/filemap: read mapping->a_ops->free_folio under i_lock memory_failure() -> ... -> filemap_remove_folio() can read mapping->a_ops after the inode has been freed. Once the folio is deleted from the pagecache it no longer pins the mapping, so after i_lock is dropped e.g., a concurrent final iput() can evict and free the inode before filemap_free_folio() looks up mapping->a_ops->free_folio. Most callers hold a reference on the inode, but not all. Documentation/filesystems/vfs.rst explicitly states that ->free_folio() must not assume the original address_space mapping still exists. Fix it by loading ->free_folio while i_lock is still held, similar to what folio_unmap_invalidate() does. Inline filemap_free_folio() into its remaining caller such that delete_from_page_cache_batch() also just loads the callback before dropping the i_lock. The bug was found by code inspection and has not been reproduced. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: get rid of filemap_free_folio() entirely; improve patch description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99733: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/truncate: look again if a folio left the mapping invalidate_inode_pages2_range() skips a folio which no lon
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/truncate: look again if a folio left the mapping invalidate_inode_pages2_range() skips a folio which no longer belongs to the mapping by the time it has got the folio lock, on the assumption that somebody else has removed it from the page cache. But the folio may have been replaced, and then there is a new folio with the same data at that index. For most cases, like folio migration, that is impossible. However, collapse_file() only checks the refcount of the old folios, under the i_pages lock, and relies on their folio locks from there on. That works for users which repeat the lookup when they find folio->mapping changed. The following scenario is, however, possible: CPU0 pwrite(O_DIRECT) CPU1 collapse_file() kiocb_invalidate_pages() read the folio (old data), lock it refcount check the write completes copy to new_folio kiocb_invalidate_post_direct_write() find_get_entries() -> old folio xas_store(new_folio) folio->mapping = NULL folio_unlock(folio) folio_lock() folio->mapping != mapping -> continue In that scenario, the collapsed folio with the data from before the write stays in the page cache after the write

items.title: CVE-2026-99734: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: make shmem_file() check the file's inode shmem_file() only checks if file->f_mapping is a shmem mapp
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: make shmem_file() check the file's inode shmem_file() only checks if file->f_mapping is a shmem mapping. This mapping can belong to another file, however, as with a Coda file backed by a tmpfs container after mmap(). So it does not guarantee that the file inode is an actual shmem inode. Seal handling and memfd preservation use this check before accessing shmem inode state, so they can access an inode of the wrong type. Let's make shmem_file() check the inode's file operations instead, to identify shmem inodes reliably. This will identify regular shmem inodes, including memfds and ordinary tmpfs files, independently of wrapper file operations. Use shmem_mapping() in collapse_file() instead to not change the behavior of collapse_file(): it operates on the page cache and uses mapping->host for shmem inode operations. Focusing on the file does not seem relevant.

items.title: CVE-2026-99735: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mglru: don't use stack pointers when walking PUD and PMD tables MGLRU passes stack copies of page-table ent
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mglru: don't use stack pointers when walking PUD and PMD tables MGLRU passes stack copies of page-table entries in walk_pud_range() and walk_pmd_range() when walking to the next level. These copies can become stale when khugepaged or MADV_DONTNEED (CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM) removes a PTE table concurrently. This pattern dates back to commit bd74fdaea146 ("mm: multi-gen LRU: support page table walks"). Likely, earlier locking masked the latent bug. Later changes exposed it: commit 1d65b771bc08 ("mm/khugepaged: retract_page_tables() without mmap or vma lock") allowed concurrent retraction, and commit cf4a65539c13 ("memcg-v1: no need for memcg locking for MGLRU") dropped the walker's outer RCU protection. The fix is simple, so just fix the original commit so we don't have to speculate. To fix it, pass the actual PMD/PUD pointers. This restores the RCU-protected lookup and validation against the live PMD. Note that the PUD handling is required as well to handle folded page tables correctly in all cases. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: handle walk_pud_range() as well, clarify+simplify de

items.title: CVE-2026-99722: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vringh: bound top-level re-entry into indirect tables In __vringh_iov(), the F_INDIRECT branch descends into t
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vringh: bound top-level re-entry into indirect tables In __vringh_iov(), the F_INDIRECT branch descends into the indirect table and continues before the descriptor accounting runs. A top-level indirect descriptor is therefore never charged to count. If such a descriptor sets NEXT to point back at itself, returning from the indirect table resumes at the same top-level descriptor, which is again not counted, so the walk never makes forward progress. Because count stays flat and indirect_count is reset to 0 on every return to the top-level table, neither bound in the loop check trips. A guest can spin the vringh worker at 100% CPU inside __vringh_iov(), an uninterruptible host DoS. Move the descriptor accounting above the indirect switch so that a top-level indirect descriptor is charged one top-level traversal step before the walk descends into its table, bringing this re-entry under the existing vrh->vring.num bound. Each top-level descriptor is still charged at most one step and indirect_count still bounds a single table, so legitimate chains (including the multiple-indirect case in tools/virtio/vringh_test.c) stay

items.title: CVE-2026-99723: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost-vdpa: fix pinned page leak in vhost_vdpa_pa_map() error path When pin_user_pages() or vhost_vdpa_map() f
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost-vdpa: fix pinned page leak in vhost_vdpa_pa_map() error path When pin_user_pages() or vhost_vdpa_map() fails, vhost_vdpa_pa_map() is supposed to unpin the pages pinned after the last successfully mapped chunk, i.e. the range [map_pfn, last_pfn]. The unpin is guarded by nchunks, but nchunks is reset to 0 every time a chunk is mapped from inside the current page list, so a failure after any such boundary leaves that pending range pinned forever. With physically scattered memory nearly every page list contains a boundary, so the leak happens on practically every failed IOTLB update. The pending range is non-empty exactly when a page has been pinned, which last_pfn already tells us, so drop nchunks and test last_pfn.

items.title: CVE-2026-99724: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ntfs: don't allow compression on volumes with clusters larger than 4K On a volume made with "mkntfs -c 8192",
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ntfs: don't allow compression on volumes with clusters larger than 4K On a volume made with "mkntfs -c 8192", a user can set FILE_ATTR_COMPRESSED on an empty file through system.ntfs_attrib. Writing to the file and reading it back after dropping the page cache then crashes: BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in ntfs_read_compressed_block+0xa2c/0x2040 Read of size 8192 at addr ffff88804355a000 by task dd/106 The read path only handles clusters up to 4K. It copies each cluster out of a single page, and a compression block of 16 8K clusters does not fit in the 64K ntfs_compression_buffer. Loading an inode already rejects compressed data on such volumes. Reject the flag change the same way.

items.title: CVE-2026-99725: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: cipso: fix optlen corruption in cipso_v4_delopt() cipso_v4_delopt() recomputes the option length by walking th
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: cipso: fix optlen corruption in cipso_v4_delopt() cipso_v4_delopt() recomputes the option length by walking the option buffer after the CIPSO option has been moved out. The walk then reads the stale bytes at the tail of the buffer as option data, and a crafted setsockopt(IP_OPTIONS) buffer can make it treat one of them as an option length, increasing opt->opt.optlen beyond the valid option data. The corrupted length stays on the socket and is later used as the copy length by getsockopt(IP_OPTIONS) and by the udp/raw/ping sendmsg paths, where it exceeds the size of the buffers they copy into. Compute the new length from the intact options before the move and subtract the CIPSO length, and fill the padding with IPOPT_END.

items.title: CVE-2026-99726: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/v3d: Widen cache_clean_lock over the whole L2TCACTL sequence v3d_clean_caches() and v3d_flush_l2t() both w
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/v3d: Widen cache_clean_lock over the whole L2TCACTL sequence v3d_clean_caches() and v3d_flush_l2t() both write the single L2TCACTL register and poll its status bits. The mutex cache_clean_lock exists to serialize them, but v3d_clean_caches() only took the lock around its final FLM_CLEAN write. These functions run concurrently: v3d_flush_l2t() is issued from the BIN/RENDER/CSD invalidate path while v3d_clean_caches() runs from the CACHE_CLEAN queue, and each queue's scheduler uses its own ordered workqueue, so their run_job callbacks execute in parallel. Because clean locked only its final write, a concurrent flush can write L2TCACTL during clean's unlocked phase. Both use non read-modify-write writes to the one register, so whichever lands last wins: clean's TMUWCF write can land on the flush's in-flight L2TFLS invalidate, triggering the GFXH-1897 hazard of writing L2TCACTL while a flush is pending. Hold cache_clean_lock across the entire L2TCACTL access sequence so it is fully mutually exclusive with v3d_flush_l2t(), which already takes the lock around its own write.

items.title: CVE-2026-99727: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: properly handle refcounted PUD mappings on fork copy_huge_pud() copies device-DAX entries with
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: properly handle refcounted PUD mappings on fork copy_huge_pud() copies device-DAX entries without taking a folio reference or updating mapcounts and the child's RSS. For example, MADV_GUARD_INSTALL sets VM_MAYBE_GUARD on a device-DAX VMA, forcing copy_page_range() to traverse the whole VMA on fork. Any remaining huge PUDs are then copied without accounting for the new mappings. Unmapping them in the child decrements accounting that was never added. Use vm_normal_page_pud() to identify refcounted mappings. Take a folio reference and add the child's PUD rmap and RSS accounting before installing the copied entry. Pass src and dst VMAs consistently instead of src and dst MM. Move the TODO.

items.title: CVE-2026-99716: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwmon: (coretemp) Set nr_cores only after core_data allocation succeeds In init_temp_data(), pdata->nr_cores i
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwmon: (coretemp) Set nr_cores only after core_data allocation succeeds In init_temp_data(), pdata->nr_cores is populated from topology_num_cores_per_package() before allocating pdata->core_data. If that allocation fails, init_temp_data() returns NULL with pdata->core_data still NULL and pdata->nr_cores set to a positive value. coretemp_add_core() logs the error without failing coretemp_cpu_online(), so the CPU still comes online with pdata->hwmon_dev registered. When the CPU is later taken offline (or the module is unloaded), coretemp_cpu_offline() calls get_temp_data(pd, cpu), which loops up to pdata->nr_cores and dereferences the NULL pdata->core_data pointer. Store the core count in a local variable and assign pdata->nr_cores only after pdata->core_data is allocated, preserving the invariant that pdata->nr_cores is zero whenever pdata->core_data is NULL.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwmon: (pmbus/q54sj108a2) Add missing NULL pointer check When CONFIG_DEBUG_FS is enabled and per-client PMBus debugfs directory creation fails during pmbus_do_probe(), q54sj108a2_probe() passes the NULL pointer returned by pmbus_get_debugfs_dir() to debugfs_create_dir() without validation, creating its debugfs directory at the debugfs root instead of under the client directory. items.title: CVE-2026-99718: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwmon: (peci/dimmtemp) Fix devres leak and UAF on concurrent unbind When a peci_dimmtemp device is unbound con
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwmon: (peci/dimmtemp) Fix devres leak and UAF on concurrent unbind When a peci_dimmtemp device is unbound concurrently with its delayed initialization work (detect_work), newly allocated devm resources and the hwmon device are leaked, leading to a use-after-free when reading the lingering hwmon sysfs attributes. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwmon: (lm87) Fix drvdata type confusion in vrm_show() and vrm_store() When an LM87 or ADM1024 device is probed with VID support enabled, reading from or writing to the vrm sysfs attribute triggers a driver data type confusion in vrm_show() and vrm_store() in drivers/hwmon/lm87.c. items.title: CVE-2026-99720: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwmon: chipcap2: fix IRQ teardown ordering The threaded IRQs are currently requested before the hwmon device i
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwmon: chipcap2: fix IRQ teardown ordering The threaded IRQs are currently requested before the hwmon device is registered. Since devres releases resources in reverse order, the hwmon device is unregistered before the IRQs are freed during driver teardown. An IRQ may therefore still run after the hwmon device has been released and access the stale data->hwmon pointer. Separate IRQ discovery from IRQ registration so that the IRQ numbers and alarm visibility flags are initialized before registering the hwmon device while the IRQs are released before the hwmon device during devres cleanup.

items.title: CVE-2026-99721: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwmon: (aquacomputer_d5next) reject short status reports The HID raw_event callback runs before HID core valid
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwmon: (aquacomputer_d5next) reject short status reports The HID raw_event callback runs before HID core validates the received report length. aqc_raw_event() reads device-specific status fields at fixed offsets, including multi-byte values, without first ensuring that the received buffer contains every field. A truncated report can therefore cause out-of-bounds reads and update hwmon state with unrelated data. The required length differs between supported devices and cannot be derived from the HID report descriptor. Define the minimum length needed by each asynchronous status format, select it while configuring the device, and reject reports that do not contain the last field accessed by that format. Keep the published length zero until probe configuration is complete, which also excludes legacy devices whose status is retrieved through feature reports.

items.title: CVE-2026-99710: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86/mmu: Cap number of parent PTEs per SP at 1000 (the arbitrary rmap limit) When potentially reusing a s
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86/mmu: Cap number of parent PTEs per SP at 1000 (the arbitrary rmap limit) When potentially reusing a shadow page, zap the shadow page if its number of parent PTEs exceeds KVM's (mostly) arbitrary rmap recycling threshold. Letting the guest create a (mostly) unbounded number of parent PTEs allows the guest to coerce KVM into creating lists containing millions of PTEs, effectively bounded only by the maximum number of shadow pages. Because PTE lists are simple singly linked lists, removal is O(n). Even worse, if a list is constructed just so, teardown can be O(n^2), e.g. if SPTEs are built such that zapping child SPTEs always zaps the last entry in the list. To cap things off, all paths that walk PTE lists do so while holding mmu_lock, without conditionally rescheduling. Using a doubly linked list would not address the issue, as removal would remain O(n) since KVM still wouldn't know where in the list to remove from. Removal could be made O(1) by storing a per-SPTE pointer, but that would largely defeat the purpose of reusing SPs, and would penalize well-behaved guests, especially for nested TDP where aliasin

items.title: CVE-2026-99711: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: nVMX: Process each host MSR entry at most once when unwinding failed VM-Entry Add a missing "break" in th
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: nVMX: Process each host MSR entry at most once when unwinding failed VM-Entry Add a missing "break" in the inner for-loop of the open coded mess that unwinds MSRs back to the pre-VM-Enter state when VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME VM-Fails due to a consistency check that is caught by hardware but missed by KVM. I.e. move on to the next MSR in the VM-Entry load list after performing a write using a value found in the VM-Exit load list. Processing *every* matching entry in the VM-Exit load list makes the processing quadratic, which is problematic if the load lists are full of MSRs that are expensive to emulate. E.g. writing APIC_BASE triggers kvm_recalculate_apic_map() and a whole pile of unnecessary work. Functionally, arbitrarily restoring the value of the first matching entry is "fine", because none of this is architecturally correct: the load lists are never supposed to have been used in the first place. In practice, it's likely a moot point as no well-behaved VMM will have multiple, diverging entries in the load lists.

items.title: CVE-2026-99712: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Conditionally resched when restarting REP string emulation When restarting emulation, e.g. of a REP-
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Conditionally resched when restarting REP string emulation When restarting emulation, e.g. of a REP-prefixed string instruction, conditionally reschedule as emulating guest writes can be deceptively slow and expensive, e.g. when shadow paging is in use and each write can trigger write tracking. In a perfect world, restarting emulation (or not) would be less arbitrary, e.g. would honor not only host events (NEED_RESCHED, signals, etc.) but also guest events (e.g. by checking kvm_vcpu_has_events()). Unfortunately, as pointed out by Sashiko, pio_in_emulated()'s read-ahead logic is baked into the restart logic, as KVM relies on restarting emulation to drain the cache and avoid duplicate reads from the I/O port. I.e. re-entering the guest on kvm_vcpu_has_events() or __xfer_to_guest_mode_work_pending() would introduce architecturally-incorrect, guest-visible changes.

items.title: CVE-2026-99713: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86/mmu: Conditionally resched when retrying gPTE walk on A/D update failure Conditionally reschedule whe
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86/mmu: Conditionally resched when retrying gPTE walk on A/D update failure Conditionally reschedule when retrying a guest PTE walk because the CMPXCHG to update A/D bits failed, e.g. because a different task/vCPU modified the relevant gPTEs. On kernels without involuntary preemption of some kind, a misbehaving guest can "capture" a pCPU effectively indefinitely and trigger soft lockups by continuously modifying its gPTEs such that the result of the walk is remains valid.

items.title: CVE-2026-99715: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvme-rdma: fix NULL queue->ctrl dereference on reconnect Since commit 2a8513091d2f ("nvme-rdma: parallelize I/
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvme-rdma: fix NULL queue->ctrl dereference on reconnect Since commit 2a8513091d2f ("nvme-rdma: parallelize I/O queue allocation and startup"), a reconnect that gets more I/O queues than before grows the tag set before the new queues are set up. queue->ctrl is only set by nvme_rdma_setup_io_queues(), so I/O submitted in between reaches nvme_rdma_queue_rq() on a queue that was never allocated and dereferences a NULL queue->ctrl: BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 000000000000034c RIP: 0010:nvme_rdma_queue_rq+0x52/0xb90 Set queue->ctrl for every queue when allocating the controller. items.title: CVE-2026-99703: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/hugetlb: fix mremap deadlock when PMD sharing is possible move_hugetlb_page_tables() holds the mapping's i_
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/hugetlb: fix mremap deadlock when PMD sharing is possible move_hugetlb_page_tables() holds the mapping's i_mmap_rwsem for write while moving hugetlb PTEs. This prevents races with truncation and protects huge_pmd_unshare(), but the move loop must not call helpers that can acquire the same rwsem for read. huge_pte_alloc() can do that when the destination can use PMD sharing: it may call huge_pmd_share(), which takes i_mmap_rwsem for read while searching for a shareable PMD table. Calling it while the move path already holds i_mmap_rwsem for write can deadlock. Avoid that path for PMD-sized hugetlb mappings that can use PMD sharing. Instead of allocating or sharing the destination page table while moving, zap the source range and let the destination fault path populate or share the PMD lazily. Reuse the hugetlb unmap logic for the source-side zap by splitting the core loop out of __unmap_hugepage_range(). The wrapper keeps the existing tlb_start_vma(), tlb_end_vma() and huge_pmd_unshare_flush() behavior, while move_hugetlb_page_tables() can reuse the unmap loop with its existing mmu_gather.

items.title: CVE-2026-99704: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares The ratios used by __wb_calc_thresh() are s
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares The ratios used by __wb_calc_thresh() are scaled to parts per million, but the threshold and ratio operands are unsigned long. On 32-bit kernels, their multiplication can wrap before the result is assigned to u64. For example, with a threshold of 25600 pages and the default maximum ratio of 1000000, wb_max_thresh becomes 4125 pages instead of 25600. The shared threshold and minimum share calculations can overflow in the same way, producing incorrect per-writeback dirty limits. Use a u64 threshold for the three ratio multiplications and div_u64() to retain the existing division order and rounding.

items.title: CVE-2026-99706: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix address wraparound when scanning large folio PTEs numa_rebuild_large_mapping() and do_swap_page() can
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix address wraparound when scanning large folio PTEs numa_rebuild_large_mapping() and do_swap_page() can be tricked into generating an address wraparound, crashing the kernel. All that's required is to map a tail page of a large folio close enough to the start/end of the address space to e.g., make unsigned long addr_start = addr - (nr << PAGE_SHIFT); to wrap around. Let's fix it by providing a better helper, folio_scan_range(), that takes care of staying within VMA and page table boundaries while handling possible wraparounds. There are some nasty details, like not being able to use pmd_addr_end() in this context. Add some helpful comments for these cases.

items.title: CVE-2026-99707: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio collapse_file() can fail its reference-cou
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio collapse_file() can fail its reference-count or dirty-folio check after unmapping with TTU_BATCH_FLUSH. Both paths put back the isolated folio, then unlock it and drop the lookup reference before reaching the common try_to_unmap_flush(). The page-cache reference does not keep the folio stable once the lock is released. Another collapse can replace and free it. With its PTEs already gone, that collapse cannot flush the first task's per-task TLB batch, and retract_page_tables() skips short or unaligned VMAs. A CPU can therefore retain a user translation to the freed folio. This has been reproduced with unprivileged MADV_COLLAPSE on a memfd. Flush at out_unlock while the lookup reference and folio lock are still held. The common flush continues to cover the accumulated pagelist on both success and rollback, preserving batching on successful collapses.

items.title: CVE-2026-99708: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ipv6: reject wrapped temporary address preferred lifetimes ipv6_create_tempaddr() raises a temporary address's
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ipv6: reject wrapped temporary address preferred lifetimes ipv6_create_tempaddr() raises a temporary address's preferred lifetime to regen_advance + age + 1 when the configured lifetime is too short. The result is stored in a u32, while regen_advance and age are unsigned long. If the sum wraps or is truncated, the stored lifetime can still be less than or equal to regen_advance + age. addrconf_verify_rtnl() then sees the new address as due for regeneration and creates another one. Temporary addresses are not limited by max_addresses since commit 4b08a8f1bd8c ("ipv6: remove max_addresses check from ipv6_create_tempaddr"), so this can cause unbounded address growth. With dad_transmits set to -1, a baseline kernel reached 2859 loopback addresses in two seconds. After storing the adjusted lifetime, verify that it is still greater than regen_advance + age. Reject the new address if the check fails. On an x86-64 KASAN kernel, the normal configuration created three IPv6 addresses. items.title: CVE-2026-99709: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: inet: frags: limit the truesize of a reassembly queue The truesize of fragments in a reassembly queue is only
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: inet: frags: limit the truesize of a reassembly queue The truesize of fragments in a reassembly queue is only bounded by the per netns ipfrag_high_thresh sysctl, which has no upper limit. inet_frag_reasm_finish() sums the truesize of all fragments in an int. If this sum reaches 2^32, it wraps, and the final sk_wmem_alloc adjustment of the socket owning the reassembled skb can cancel its own reference, leading to a use-after-free of this socket. This can be triggered from an unprivileged user/network namespace, raising ipfrag_high_thresh and using padded TUN packets, which keep a large truesize after being trimmed by ip_rcv_core(). Track the sum of the truesize of fragments in each queue, and refuse a fragment that would make it bigger than INT_MAX / 2. Callers kill the queue on this error. This bound is far above the needs of legitimate traffic.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ocfs2: find the xattr entry again after defragmenting a bucket ocfs2_xattr_set_entry_bucket() hands loc.xl_entry to ocfs2_xa_set() twice: once for the bucket as it stands, and, if that reports -ENOSPC, once more after ocfs2_defrag_xattr_bucket() has packed the name/value pairs down. items.title: CVE-2026-99697: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: memcontrol: fix NULL pointer deref and UAF from high_work_func() on dying memcg When memory.high is exceed
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: memcontrol: fix NULL pointer deref and UAF from high_work_func() on dying memcg When memory.high is exceeded in non-task context, try_charge_memcg() schedules memcg->high_work without taking a reference on the memcg, and high_work_func() invokes reclaim_high() without pinning the memcg. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved at a fixed address CMA areas allocated from memblock have their memory accepted by memblock_alloc_range_nid(), but areas reserved at a fixed address with memblock_reserve() are not. If a fixed CMA area is requested by the cma= @ command line parameter, it may be in regular RAM and on TDX and SEV-SNP guests it must be accepted. items.title: CVE-2026-99700: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/hugetlb_vmemmap: map the shared tail page writable page_ref_add_unless_zero() reads the refcount and then u
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/hugetlb_vmemmap: map the shared tail page writable page_ref_add_unless_zero() reads the refcount and then updates it with a cmpxchg. A lockless get, such as a page cache lookup or a PFN scanner, can read a non-zero refcount from a page that is then freed and reused as a hugetlb tail page. If HVO remaps its struct page to the shared tail page in between, the cmpxchg writes to read-only vmemmap: CPU0 (lockless get) CPU1 c = atomic_read(&page->_refcount) page freed page allocated as a hugetlb tail HVO remaps the struct page RO try_cmpxchg(&page->_refcount, &c, c + 1) -> write fault on read-only vmemmap The refcount is zero by then and the compare fails, but a compare-and-swap instruction needs write access whether or not it succeeds. Commit bd225530a4c7 ("mm/hugetlb_vmemmap: fix race with speculative PFN walkers") closed the window with RCU on both sides. items.title: CVE-2026-99701: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: fix userfaultfd protection during merge and unmerge KSM loses userfaultfd protection when replace_page
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: fix userfaultfd protection during merge and unmerge KSM loses userfaultfd protection when replace_page() builds a new PTE from vma->vm_page_prot. Dropping its uffd bit lets a subsequent write go through ordinary COW instead of userfaultfd write protection handling. For RWP, a merged page also becomes readable without faulting. Keeping the uffd bit and restoring PAGE_NONE fixes merging, but we also have to handle unmerging. An existing KSM page can be protected with RWP before MADV_UNMERGEABLE, so unmerging already needs fixing independently of preserving RWP during merging. Unsharing replaces a shared page with a private one and should leave userfaultfd protection in place, as do_wp_page() already does for write protection. Currently, an unshare fault reaches do_uffd_rwp() before it can proceed to do_wp_page(). - With synchronous RWP, handle_userfault() returns VM_FAULT_SIGBUS. break_ksm() then reports success with a KSM page still merged. - With asynchronous RWP, protection is cleared before unsharing. Preserve the uffd bit when merging, and restore PAGE_NONE for RWP. Let FAULT_FLAG_UNSHARE skip RWP fault

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: write lock source VMA before duplicating it in __split_vma() __split_vma() duplicates the source VMA before taking its VMA write lock, and until the VMA is write-locked, a concurrent thread might set VMA_MAYBE_GUARD_BIT, resulting in the duplication missing the flag. That is outside the __counted_by_le(xh_count) bounds of xh_entries[] and lands on the header, so the value picked up is xh_count | xh_free_start << 16. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ocfs2: find the xattr entry again after converting a block to a bucket ocfs2_xattr_create_index_block() turns a non-indexed xattr block into a tree by copying it into a bucket, and the copy sorts the entries: a block holds them in insertion order, a bucket by name hash. ocfs2_xattr_update_xattr_search() nevertheless relocates the caller's search by the index the entry had in the block, so unless the two orders agreed it points at an unrelated entry, and nothing between there and the write compares that entry's name with the one being set. Setting an xattr whose new value no longer fits the block arrives here with xs->not_found clear. The block gave up because ocfs2_xa_block_can_reuse() wants an exact namevalue size match, while ocfs2_xa_bucket_can_reuse() only wants an entry at least as large as the new one, so the bucket accepts a pair the block rejected and the update lands on whichever entry the sort left at that index. items.title: CVE-2026-99682: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: virtio_blk: use synchronous quiesce in virtblk_freeze_priv() blk_mq_run_work_fn() can call blk_mq_sched_dispat
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: virtio_blk: use synchronous quiesce in virtblk_freeze_priv() blk_mq_run_work_fn() can call blk_mq_sched_dispatch_requests() through blk_mq_run_dispatch_ops(). The dispatcher checks QUEUE_FLAG_QUIESCED while the flag is clear. It can then be preempted before it gets a request. At that time, it has no queue usage reference, so blk_mq_freeze_queue() does not wait for it. virtblk_freeze_priv() then calls blk_mq_quiesce_queue_nowait() and blk_mq_unfreeze_queue(). A new request can enter the queue. The old dispatcher can run again, use its old flag check, get the new request, and call virtio_queue_rq(). At the same time, virtblk_freeze_priv() can reset the device, delete the virtqueues, and free vblk->vqs. The old dispatcher can then use a deleted virtqueue or a NULL vblk->vqs, and the kernel can crash. Fix this by using blk_mq_quiesce_queue(), which waits for dispatch code that was already running. Keep the existing freeze and unfreeze order. The queue remains quiesced until virtblk_restore_priv() calls blk_mq_unquiesce_queue().

items.title: CVE-2026-99683: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vduse: fix VA/PA confusion in the coherent page fault path vduse_domain_get_coherent_page() assumes that iotlb
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vduse: fix VA/PA confusion in the coherent page fault path vduse_domain_get_coherent_page() assumes that iotlb entries above bounce_size were installed by vduse_domain_alloc_coherent(), so it treats map->addr as a physical address. But vduse registers with use_va = true, and when the device is bound to vhost_vdpa, vhost_vdpa_va_map() stores a userspace virtual address in map->addr, which vduse_domain_set_map() then copies into the same iotlb. A process holding the domain file descriptor across a rebind can therefore fault in an arbitrary physical page with read/write access, ignoring the entry permissions. Additionally, since the domain file mmap lacks VM_IO, the domain file itself can be mapped and passed to vhost_vdpa_va_map(), producing self-referential entries that bypass the coherent path check. To fix, only translate entries whose backing file is the domain file itself in vduse_domain_get_coherent_page(), reject such entries in vduse_domain_set_map() since only external mappings should be imported, and set VM_IO on the domain file mmap so vhost_vdpa_va_map() refuses to map it in the first place.

items.title: CVE-2026-99684: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwrng: virtio - prevent use-after-free after a failed restore remove_common() frees the driver data during fre
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwrng: virtio - prevent use-after-free after a failed restore remove_common() frees the driver data during freeze, but does not clear vdev->priv, which points to freed memory. If probe_common() then fails during restore, a later remove or freeze can dereference the dangling pointer. Clear vdev->priv on the probe_common() error cleanup path and before freeing the driver data in remove_common(). Also reset the device and return early from remove_common() if vdev->priv is already NULL for a safe teardown after a failed restore.

items.title: CVE-2026-99685: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommu/virtio: Reset device before deleting virtqueues on probe failure viommu_probe() marks the device DRIVER_
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommu/virtio: Reset device before deleting virtqueues on probe failure viommu_probe() marks the device DRIVER_OK before populating the event virtqueue and registering the IOMMU device in sysfs. viommu_fill_evtq() hands the device a set of device-writable buffers through virtqueue_add_inbuf(), so from that point on the device may write into them and into the rings. If either step fails, the error path deletes the virtqueues without resetting the device first. The event buffers are allocated with devm_kmalloc_array() and are released as probe unwinds, so the device can go on writing to memory that has been freed. Reset the device before deleting the virtqueues, the way viommu_remove() already does.

items.title: CVE-2026-99686: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost: fix used ring index wrap in vhost_add_used_n_in_order vhost_add_used_n_in_order() advances start by nhe
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost: fix used ring index wrap in vhost_add_used_n_in_order vhost_add_used_n_in_order() advances start by nheads[i] but wraps it with a single subtraction. If start + nheads[i] >= 2 * vq->num, start can remain outside the ring. With used-ring logging enabled, start > vq->num makes (vq->num - start) underflow. log_write() then sets bits beyond the dirty-log bitmap, potentially corrupting adjacent userspace memory. This is reachable on the vhost-net TX path with VIRTIO_F_IN_ORDER: done_idx can reach VHOST_NET_BATCH (64), triggering the issue with a 32-entry ring. Wrap start with a mask to keep it within the ring. VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM enforces a nonzero power-of-two ring size, allowing start to be wrapped using & (vq->num - 1).

items.title: CVE-2026-99687: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost-scsi: zero misaligned I/O bounce pages The misaligned I/O fallback copies the full bounce scatterlist to
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost-scsi: zero misaligned I/O bounce pages The misaligned I/O fallback copies the full bounce scatterlist to the request buffer during completion. If a data-in command transfers less than requested, part of a newly allocated bounce page can remain unwritten. Allocate bounce pages with __GFP_ZERO so all bytes copied during completion have a defined value. This path is already the slow fallback for misaligned I/O, so the added initialization cost is acceptable. Found during an LLM-assisted source audit and validated with a QEMU/KVM vhost-scsi target using misaligned data-in commands.

items.title: CVE-2026-99688: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/sched: sch_qfq: prevent aggregate self-replacement qfq_change_class() snapshots the current aggregate sett
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/sched: sch_qfq: prevent aggregate self-replacement qfq_change_class() snapshots the current aggregate settings while holding the qdisc tree lock, but drops the lock before selecting the destination aggregate. During that gap, qfq_enqueue() can move the class to an aggregate matching the requested settings. When qfq_change_class() resumes, qfq_find_agg() then returns cl->agg. If it is a singleton, qfq_deact_rm_from_agg() frees the aggregate before qfq_add_to_agg() immediately accesses the same pointer, causing a use-after-free. While holding the tree lock, skip the replacement when the destination is already the current aggregate. Any estimator replacement has already completed, so the class change can finish normally.

items.title: CVE-2026-99689: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: fix temporary cursor leak in btree shift corruption paths In xfs_btree_lshift and xfs_btree_rshift, when
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: fix temporary cursor leak in btree shift corruption paths In xfs_btree_lshift and xfs_btree_rshift, when XFS_IS_CORRUPT detects an invalid firstrec/lastrec result after xfs_btree_dup_cursor has successfully allocated a temporary cursor, the error path jumps to error0 which returns without freeing tcur. This leaks the cursor memory, the xfs_group reference, and the per-level buffer references held by the duplicated cursor. Jump to error1 instead, which calls xfs_btree_del_cursor(tcur, XFS_BTREE_ERROR) to properly release all resources.

items.title: CVE-2026-99674: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: dev: can_dropped_invalid_skb: drop CAN XL frames on non-CAN XL devices Sending a PF_PACKET bypasses the C
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: dev: can_dropped_invalid_skb: drop CAN XL frames on non-CAN XL devices Sending a PF_PACKET bypasses the CAN framework logic and can directly reach a CAN driver's xmit() function. The PF_PACKET framework only checks that skb->len does not exceed the net_device MTU. For a CAN device that is not CAN XL capable, anything above CANFD_MTU (72 bytes) is therefore dropped before it reaches the driver. However, CAN XL frames are variable length. can_is_canxl_skb() accepts lengths in the range CANXL_HDR_SIZE + CANXL_MIN_DLEN up to CANXL_MTU, i.e. 13 to 2060 bytes. As a result, an ETH_P_CANXL skb with a length between 13 and 72 bytes can pass both the MTU and the can_dropped_invalid_skb() checks. A driver that does not support CAN XL will interpret canxl_frame->flags as a length because of the overlap with can_frame->len. And because CANXL_XLF is set, the resulting length is between 128 and 255. For drivers that do not check can_frame->len before copying can_frame->data, as most drivers do, this results in a buffer overflow of up to 247 bytes. Drop ETH_P_CANXL skbs if the device does not have the CAN_CAP_XL capability. K

items.title: CVE-2026-99675: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: reject keep-alive timeouts that would overflow nvmet_set_feat_kato() and nvmet_alloc_ctrl() convert the
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: reject keep-alive timeouts that would overflow nvmet_set_feat_kato() and nvmet_alloc_ctrl() convert the 32-bit millisecond KATO from the host to seconds with DIV_ROUND_UP(kato, 1000). The addition in DIV_ROUND_UP() is done in 32 bits, so any KATO above 4294966296 ms wraps around and rounds to 0 seconds. A Set Features command with KATO 0xffffffff then succeeds but disables the keep-alive timer: Get Features returns 0 and Keep Alive fails with Keep Alive Timeout Invalid. A Connect command with such a KATO creates a controller without a keep-alive timer. The converted value has more consumers that can overflow. Get Features multiplies it by 1000, and the timer paths multiply it by HZ in 32 bits and arm a delay that must not exceed MAX_JIFFY_OFFSET. Reject a KATO whose rounded value does not fit all of these. Return Keep Alive Timeout Invalid from both Set Features and Connect. Validate Set Features before stopping the current timer so a failed update leaves its timeout unchanged. Round in 64 bits. A KATO of 0 keeps its current meaning.

items.title: CVE-2026-99676: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: restore refcount ordering for lockless socket access Before commit fb041bb7c0a9 ("locking/refcount: Conso
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: restore refcount ordering for lockless socket access Before commit fb041bb7c0a9 ("locking/refcount: Consolidate implementations of refcount_t"), default builds implemented refcount_inc_not_zero() using atomic_add_unless(), which provided full memory ordering on success. The commit removed that ordering on weakly ordered architectures, allowing accesses after a successful reference acquisition to be reordered before it. Use refcount_inc_not_zero_acquire() in the IPv4 and IPv6 established lookups and in inet_twsk_purge(), where the socket is validated again after taking a reference. bpf_sk_assign() can receive a socket pointer obtained through BTF without a reference. Use acquire ordering when it takes its own reference for a refcounted socket. Use refcount_set_release() when setting refcounts in the SYN cookie, TCP Fast Open, request migration, and TIME_WAIT paths. Keep the existing TIME_WAIT smp_wmb(), which separately orders the refcount store before ehash publication.

items.title: CVE-2026-99677: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: clamp the pNFS layout range to the maximum file size xfs_fs_map_blocks() lets two bad layout ranges throu
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: clamp the pNFS layout range to the maximum file size xfs_fs_map_blocks() lets two bad layout ranges through. An offset of 2^63 or more is negative and passes "offset > limit". A length above the limit, such as NFS4_UINT64_MAX, wraps "offset > limit - length" and stays unclamped. With NFS4_UINT64_MAX, a read layout is built from an uninitialized mapping. Reject a negative offset and one at the limit, and clamp the length. This needs "xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent".

items.title: CVE-2026-99678: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent xfs_iomap_write_direct() reserves blocks fo
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent xfs_iomap_write_direct() reserves blocks for the whole count in an unsigned int. For a pNFS layout the client chooses that count, and an RW LAYOUTGET for 16 TiB wraps the reservation and shuts XFS down. xfs_bmapi_write() maps at most XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN blocks here, so cap the count at that. nfsd asks again for the rest. The other callers get the same mapping as before.

items.title: CVE-2026-99679: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT, becaus
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT, because nfsd does not check the extents against its layouts. xfs_iomap_write_unwritten() then allocates written blocks there. A large hole overruns the block reservation and shuts XFS down. A small one exposes stale data. Refuse such a range with -EIO, using XFS_BMAPI_CONVERT_ONLY.

items.title: CVE-2026-99680: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode XFS_DIFLA
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode XFS_DIFLAG_PREALLOC only when it allocates blocks for a write layout. A write layout past EOF can also hand out allocated blocks, such as speculative preallocation. blockgc then frees them under the layout, and another file may get them. Mark the inode whenever a write mapping ends past EOF.

items.title: CVE-2026-99681: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: blk-mq: fix out-of-bounds read in blk_mq_free_rqs A KASAN slab-out-of-bounds read can occur in blk_mq_free_rqs
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: blk-mq: fix out-of-bounds read in blk_mq_free_rqs A KASAN slab-out-of-bounds read can occur in blk_mq_free_rqs() when there is a mismatch between the number of hardware queues allocated for the IO scheduler (et->nr_hw_queues) and the number of hardware queues in the block tag set (set->nr_hw_queues). This mismatch can happen if blk_mq_update_nr_hw_queues() fails halfway through (e.g., due to memory pressure during blk_mq_prealloc_tag_set_tags()). In this error path, the elevator is restored with a larger number of hardware queues than the block tag set actually has. When the elevator is later freed, blk_mq_free_sched_tags() iterates up to the new et->nr_hw_queues and calls blk_mq_free_rqs(). In blk_mq_free_rqs(), it attempts to access set->tags[hctx_idx] to get the driver tags. Because set->nr_hw_queues was not updated due to the earlier failure, set->tags still has the old (smaller) size, leading to an out-of-bounds read. items.title: CVE-2026-99667: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() drops the
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() drops the PTE lock after it has cleared the page table, and takes the PMD lock and the PTE lock to remove it. In between, MADV_DONTNEED with CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM can reclaim the page table. The pmd_same() check is supposed to handle this, but it is only done with CONFIG_SPLIT_PTE_PTLOCKS. Fix it by performing the check unconditionally. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: adjust description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99668: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: fix zapping migration entries for device-private THPs A PMD migration entry can refer to a dev
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: fix zapping migration entries for device-private THPs A PMD migration entry can refer to a device-private folio. zap_huge_pmd_folio() checks the folio type instead of the entry type, so it treats such a migration entry as a device-private entry. Installing the migration entry already removed the reverse mapping and dropped the mapping reference. Zapping it must not repeat those operations. Concurrent MADV_DONTNEED during migration back to system memory can trigger this. Check the PMD entry type using pmd_is_device_private_entry(). Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99669: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: fix truncate racing with PMD zapping zap_huge_pmd_folio() removes the rmap before calling foli
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: fix truncate racing with PMD zapping zap_huge_pmd_folio() removes the rmap before calling folio_mark_dirty(). If this was the last mapping, truncation can skip unmapping the folio and proceed without waiting for the PMD lock, racing with dirtying. ifs_set_range_dirty() can oops if MADV_DONTNEED races with ftruncate() on XFS, when we get the folio set dirty after it was found to not be mapped anymore. Move folio_mark_dirty() and folio_mark_accessed() before rmap removal, matching the PTE zap path. This keeps the folio mapped while updating its state, so truncation must wait for the page table lock. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify comment and description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99670: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: dev: can_fill_info(): don't wake up controller if interface is down If the interface is down, the CAN con
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: dev: can_fill_info(): don't wake up controller if interface is down If the interface is down, the CAN controller might be powered down and its clocks gated. Don't call do_get_berr_counter() to read the bus error counters if the interface is down, and adjust can_get_size() to match. This removes one trigger for a synchronous external abort seen on i.MX8QXP when "ip link show" is run on a flexcan interface that was never brought up. The underlying cause is platform-specific: on i.MX8QXP the CAN clocks are gated through the SCU LPCG and the subsystem shares the IMX_SC_R_CAN_0 power domain, and there is a window after pm_runtime_resume_and_get() returns where the clock has not reached the module yet. This patch avoids the netlink query path while the interface is down, but does not root-cause the LPCG window itself. As a result, IFLA_CAN_BERR_COUNTER is no longer reported for down interfaces. Userspace must treat the attribute as optional. The issue was triggered on an i.MX8QXP board by running "ip link show" without ever bringing the interface up: Internal error: synchronous external abort: 0000000096000210 pc :

items.title: CVE-2026-99671: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock() The CAN_RAW and CAN_ISOTP specific socket options
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock() The CAN_RAW and CAN_ISOTP specific socket options are copied from and to user space while holding lock_sock(). CAN_ISOTP only copies its options for unbound sockets, which isotp_notify() skips without taking lock_sock(). items.title: CVE-2026-99672: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock The receive lists of a CAN device are located in the dev
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock The receive lists of a CAN device are located in the device's can_ml_priv and travel with the device when it is moved to another network namespace. items.title: CVE-2026-99673: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: replace ARPHRD_CAN type checks with can_get_ml_priv() Commit 4e096a18867a ("net: introduce CAN specific p
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: replace ARPHRD_CAN type checks with can_get_ml_priv() Commit 4e096a18867a ("net: introduce CAN specific pointer in the struct net_device") introduced an explicit way to assign the midlayer private pointer (dev->ml_priv) to named users like ML_PRIV_CAN.
