The referenced commit only converted the j1939 and proc code to this check, while the other parts of the CAN subsystem still rely on dev->type == ARPHRD_CAN. The TUNSETLINK ioctl allows a down TUN/TAP device to set its hardware type to ARPHRD_CAN while dev->ml_priv remains NULL. Such a repurposed netdevice passes the ARPHRD_CAN checks. Commit 8aa59e355949 ("can: af_can: fix NULL pointer dereference in can_rx_register()") already made can_rx_register() reject such devices. But can_rx_unregister() still only checks dev->type and dereferences the NULL ml_priv when it walks the receive lists of the device. CAN_ISOTP reaches this path: isotp_bind() ignores the return values of can_rx_register() and binds the socket anyway. When the socket is released or the device is unregistered, i

items.title: CVE-2026-99660: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering userfaultfd_unregister() wakes pen
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering userfaultfd_unregister() wakes pending missing faults before clearing the VMA's userfaultfd registration. With per-VMA fault locking, holding mmap_lock for write does not prevent another fault from queuing after the wakeup but before userfaultfd_clear_vma() write-locks the VMA. That waiter can then remain asleep indefinitely. Call vma_start_write() before waking waiters. Existing fault handlers queue themselves before dropping the VMA read lock, and new readers are excluded until mmap_write_unlock().

items.title: CVE-2026-99661: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast The overflow check in gup_fast_fallba
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast The overflow check in gup_fast_fallback() only covers the addition to start. The preceding nr_pages << PAGE_SHIFT can already have truncated the length on 32bit. Users such as RapidIO's rio_dma_transfer() can derive such page counts from a 64-bit userspace length. Let's just check_shl_overflow() to reject any such overflow with -EOVERFLOW early.

items.title: CVE-2026-99662: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its pa
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its page table walk and can write past the caller's page array. The old end <= start check caught empty ranges, but was replaced with an overflow check. Users such as OrangeFS can pass a zero page count derived from a userspace-supplied length. So let's return zero for nr_pages == 0 before starting the walk, just like GUP-slow. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99663: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios obtained directly from the pa
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios obtained directly from the page cache without checking whether they are uptodate. However, shmem fallocate() can leave newly allocated folios uncleared and not uptodate. Callers such as udmabuf can then expose uninitialized memory to userspace. Clear non-uptodate folios and mark them uptodate under the folio lock before returning them to the caller. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description and comment ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99664: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: recheck the PUD under PTL in follow_pud_mask() follow_pud_mask() reads the PUD without a lock. If it i
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: recheck the PUD under PTL in follow_pud_mask() follow_pud_mask() reads the PUD without a lock. If it is a leaf, it takes the lock and calls follow_huge_pud(), which reads the entry again, but only tests whether it is present. A leaf can be zapped concurrently and a page fault can fill the empty entry with a page table. This currently only applies when device-dax makes use of PUD entries, and the fault after e.g., MADV_DONTNEED would find THPs to be disabled. That requires a sequence like 1) Fault in the PUD 2) Disable THP 3) Have GUP race against concurrent MADV_DONTNEED + refault Which is rather unlikely to happen in practice, which is why we never received a report about such a problem. Before commit 1b1676180246 ("mm/gup: handle huge pud for follow_pud_mask()"), we performed that check in follow_devmap_pud() by testing for pud_devmap(). Let's fix it by just structuring follow_pud_mask() similar to follow_pmd_mask(), minus protnone stuff that does not apply and minus FOLL_SPLIT_PMD handling. That makes it much easier to spot any such inconsistencies. Perform the pud_bad() check early in follow_pmd_mask()

items.title: CVE-2026-99665: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: preserve dirty bits when collapsing PTE-mapped THPs try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() clears PTEs w
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: preserve dirty bits when collapsing PTE-mapped THPs try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() clears PTEs without transferring their dirty bits to the folio. A shmem read fault can map a clean folio writable, so a later store only dirties the PTE. Losing that dirty bit allows reclaim to discard modified data. The assumption that regular files are read-only is also obsolete since commit 1b6444331bebb ("mm/khugepaged: enable clean pagecache folio collapse for writable files"). In any case, transferring PTE dirty bits to the folio when removing mappings (and while the folio is still mapped) is the right thing to do. Use get_and_clear_ptes() to collect the dirty bits and mark the folio dirty before unmapping it. Update the comment. This was reproduced with shmem using MADV_COLLAPSE followed by MADV_PAGEOUT. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: adjust comment; simplify description; cover file-thp as well ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99666: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: fix PMD table lock leak in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() For a private mapping with userfaultfd
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: fix PMD table lock leak in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() For a private mapping with userfaultfd, try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() takes the PMD table lock before it maps the page table for the second time. If that (pte_offset_map_rw_nolock) fails, because the page table vanished in the meantime due to concurrent page table reclaim, it leaves through the abort label, where the PMD table lock is unlocked if it differs from PTE table lock. In case the PMD table lock and the PTE table lock match, which is the case without CONFIG_SPLIT_PTE_PTLOCKS after pte_offset_map_rw_nolock() failed, we miss to unlock the PMD table. To fix it, forget the PTE table lock when we unmap+unlock the PTE table. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: move the ptl = NULL handling; rewrite description, drop wrong comments ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99653: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unkillable fault loop on MAP_DROPPABLE memory handle_mm_fault() suppresses VM_FAULT_OOM for VM_DROPPAB
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unkillable fault loop on MAP_DROPPABLE memory handle_mm_fault() suppresses VM_FAULT_OOM for VM_DROPPABLE mappings. For user-mode faults, pending signals are processed before retrying the access. Kernel-mode faults on user buffers instead return directly to the faulting instruction. With persistent allocation failures (esp. memcg limits), a syscall, such as write(), can therefore loop while not dropping locks. Only suppress VM_FAULT_OOM when FAULT_FLAG_USER is set, allowing kernel-mode faults and GUP to fail and signal allocation errors. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99654: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unmap_mapping_range() beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit Commit 9eab0421fa94 ("mm: fix unmap_mapping_range high bi
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unmap_mapping_range() beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit Commit 9eab0421fa94 ("mm: fix unmap_mapping_range high bits shift bug") made holebegin and holelen unsigned before they are shifted, by casting them to pgoff_t. That is an unsigned long: on a 32-bit kernel the cast cuts off the upper half of the two loff_t values, so a hole which begins at 4 GiB or beyond is taken for one in the first 4 GiB of the file. truncate_pagecache() passes the new size of the file and asks for private COWed pages to be unmapped as well. If a file of 6 GiB is truncated to 5 GiB, everything from 1 GiB on is unmapped, and what a process has written to a private mapping of the range between 1 GiB and 5 GiB is lost: it reads the contents of the file again. Where the range has an end, the wrong range is unmapped instead of the right one. The page cache copes with that, as it unmaps every folio that it removes. The callers which only have unmap_mapping_range() to get rid of user mappings do not, for example drm_vma_node_unmap(), whose fake offsets reach beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit, and revoke_iomem() with physical addresses of more than 32 bits. items.title: CVE-2026-99655: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory: reject remote COW faults on PFN mappings When handling a COW fault without a normal source page (PF
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory: reject remote COW faults on PFN mappings When handling a COW fault without a normal source page (PFN mappings), __wp_page_copy_user() copies from the faulting user address. For remote faults, this accesses the wrong address space, resulting in wrong data getting copied. For example, user_events updates an enable bit in the registering process's memory. If that memory needs to be faulted in, user_event_enabler_fault_fixup() calls fixup_user_fault() from a work item. Placing the enable bit in a private PFN mapping can trigger this remote COW path. Reject these faults with VM_FAULT_SIGBUS when the target mm differs from current->mm: remote faults. Ordinary (non-PFN) mappings are not affected. The user-address copy dates back to commit 6aab341e0a28 ("mm: re-architect the VM_UNPAGED logic"); likely, actual ways to get remote faults in there on COW PFN mappings appeared afterwards. But the fix is simple and straight forward. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify comment and description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99656: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/madvise: fix data loss from MADV_FREE on a KSM page MADV_FREE can clear the dirty flag of a singly mapped K
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/madvise: fix data loss from MADV_FREE on a KSM page MADV_FREE can clear the dirty flag of a singly mapped KSM folio. The folio remains in the stable tree and can gain new mappings without being dirtied again. Once marked lazyfree, reclaim can discard data that those mappings still need. KSM always marks a folio dirty when converting it to a KSM folio in try_to_merge_one_page(). Marking a folio lazyfree clears PG_swapbacked but leaves PG_dirty unchanged. Preserving PG_dirty makes reclaim restore PG_swapbacked instead of discarding the folio. This also protects folios that were already lazyfree when KSM converted them. Skip KSM folios before clearing their dirty flag, checking under the folio lock to serialize with KSM conversion.

items.title: CVE-2026-99657: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab() Radeon uses a non-NULL notifier->mm to decide whether to call mm
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab() Radeon uses a non-NULL notifier->mm to decide whether to call mmu_interval_notifier_remove() when freeing a buffer object. __mmu_interval_notifier_insert() sets ->mm before validating the range, so a wrapping userptr range can leave ->mm set after insertion fails. Cleanup then tries to remove an unregistered notifier for which no mm reference was acquired. Set ->mm only after mmgrab(), once insertion can no longer fail. While we could fix radeon's code instead, setting ->mm on success only makes the code more robust. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99658: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error When an ordinary MMU notifier rejects a no
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error When an ordinary MMU notifier rejects a non-blocking invalidation, the interval invalidation started beforehand is left unfinished: the caller skips mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_end(). Subsequent interval notifier operations can then wait forever. The only in-tree trigger is nouveau SVM, which uses both notifier types and rejects non-blocking invalidations. Reaping via the OOM reaper or process_mrelease() can therefore leave the GPU fault worker stuck, holding a reference that prevents the dying process's address space and memory from being freed. End the interval invalidation when an ordinary notifier fails a non-blocking invalidation, like mn_itree_invalidate() already does when an interval notifier fails. Make that handling clearer in the documentation of mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_start_nonblock(). Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: simplify description, update function doc ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99659: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger __tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger __tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which has to be flushed as an unsigned int. Its callers, tlb_flush_{pte,pmd,pud,p4d}_range(), get and pass an unsigned long. Consequently, a range that is 4 GiB or larger gets truncated, possibly to 0. On arm64 with hugetlb, a 64k kernel can have 16 GiB hugetlb folios mapped contiguously at the PMD level and flush them when unmapping, and a 16k kernel can flush 64 GiB PUDs through tlb_unshare_pmd_ptdesc(). So at least these two scenarios are affected. Fix it by flushing the proper range instead of the truncated one by properly using "unsigned long" for range_size. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: use two-tab indent, simplify description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99645: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use When a driver calls dma_free_contiguous() before quiescing DMA, t
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use When a driver calls dma_free_contiguous() before quiescing DMA, the page might still have a reference from the device. put_page_testzero() there returns false, WARN fires, but the code proceeds to free_contig_frozen_range() putting a live page onto buddy and clearing the bitmap. A subsequent allocation can hand the same PFN to a new owner while the original holder still references it. A concurrent put_page() that drops the last reference between the testzero loop and free_contig_frozen_range() can double-queue the page via page->lru, corrupting buddy lists. Avoid the corruption by not freeing a CMA region if any of the pages inside are still in use. Make it explicit in the warning that the driver allowed a leak. While at it, use page_ref_freeze() to make the semantics clearer and switch to pr_warn_ratelimited(). [ david: use page_ref_freeze() + pr_warn_ratelimited() ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99646: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: don't leak the charge for stack growth acct_stack_growth() charges stack expansion even without VM_ACC
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: don't leak the charge for stack growth acct_stack_growth() charges stack expansion even without VM_ACCOUNT. This can happen for read-only or MAP_NORESERVE mappings created with MAP_GROWSDOWN. Unmapping these VMAs does not release the charge, leaking Committed_AS. Only check and charge growth for VM_ACCOUNT VMAs, matching mremap(). Unaccounted growth skips the overcommit check while remaining subject to the other stack-growth limits.

items.title: CVE-2026-99647: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: split huge PUDs when adjusting VMA boundaries PFN mappings such as VFIO PCI BAR mappings can u
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: split huge PUDs when adjusting VMA boundaries PFN mappings such as VFIO PCI BAR mappings can use PUD leaves while allowing VMA splits at page granularity. However, vma_adjust_trans_huge() only handles PMDs. After faulting a writable PUD-sized VFIO BAR mapping, changing its first page to read-only with mprotect() makes the PMD walk treat the PUD leaf as a PMD table. Applying MADV_DONTFORK to the first PMD-sized chunk leaves the PUD spanning two VMAs: the PMD-aligned boundary skips splitting. Walk the page tables once at each adjusted boundary and split a huge PUD or PMD leaf as needed. Handle PUD leaves even when the boundary is PMD-aligned.

items.title: CVE-2026-99648: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: call ->may_split() before a partial merge A driver can use the ->may_split() hook to forbid a VMA boun
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: call ->may_split() before a partial merge A driver can use the ->may_split() hook to forbid a VMA boundary at certain addresses. A device-dax device is a character device that gives raw access to a range of memory through mmap(). device-dax refuses any address that is not a multiple of the device's alignment through vm_ops->may_split. vma_merge_existing_range() can move boundaries, but does not call vm_ops->may_split. If a range at the edge of a VMA gets the attributes of the adjacent VMA, the function moves only that range over to the neighbour: one VMA shrinks and the other grows. This is a partial merge, and vma_modify() tries it before any split. Take a device-dax VMA that lies next to another VMA of the same file. The user calls mprotect() on the one page of the first VMA that touches the second VMA, and asks for the protection that the second VMA already has. The result is a partial merge. It puts the boundary inside a 1 GiB mapping, which is a single leaf entry at the PUD level. As part of the merge, the kernel looks for a huge PMD to split at the new boundary. items.title: CVE-2026-99649: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: check large swap-cache folios before mapping them KSM folios are always small, but their shared swap s
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: check large swap-cache folios before mapping them KSM folios are always small, but their shared swap slots can be read back as part of a large folio in the swap cache. ksm_might_need_to_copy() skips large folios, so another process can map a page with an incompatible anon_vma or page index. Reverse mapping then cannot find the new mapping, preventing migration or reclaim. Apply the same compatibility checks to large folios as to small ones. Pass the page corresponding to the swap entry and copy only that page when necessary. In do_swap_page()'s copy path, decrement only that slot's swap count, because the source swap-cache folio can now be large. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

items.title: CVE-2026-99650: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: fix use of a freed anon_vma at swap-in A folio read from a swap slot previously shared by KSM can rema
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: fix use of a freed anon_vma at swap-in A folio read from a swap slot previously shared by KSM can remain in the swap cache after the process that first mapped it exits. Its anon_vma can then be freed, so ksm_might_need_to_copy() must not dereference it to compare roots. Doing so can result in some false-positives, resulting in the reverse mapping missing the new folio mapping, preventing migration and reclaim. SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU allows individual anon_vma objects to be reused immediately after freeing. A stale pointer can then refer to another anon_vma whose root matches, even though the target VMA is not linked to that anon_vma. Move the anonymous rmap compatibility checks into folio_anon_rmap_compatible(). Keep the page-index check and compare the folio's anon_vma pointer against the VMA's own anon_vma and root first. If neither matches, bite the bullet and walk the VMA's anon_vma_chain. The VMA keeps these anon_vmas alive, and finding a match guarantees that reverse mapping can find the new mapping. Lorenzo Stoakes says in a private discussion: "This isn't quite equivalent to the existing check. Every

items.title: CVE-2026-99651: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes Each full scan resets ksm_nr_node_ids unstable tree roots. Enabl
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes Each full scan resets ksm_nr_node_ids unstable tree roots. Enabling merge_across_nodes resets this count to 1, even if per-node roots were previously allocated. So when toggling "merge_across_nodes" 0 -> 1 -> 0, a scan that starts while the setting is 1 and continues after switching back to 0 can encounter stale unstable tree roots, resulting in UAF. Only root is allowed to change "merge_across_nodes", and the documented sequence is: "merge_across_nodes setting can be changed only when there are no ksm shared pages in the system: set run 2 to unmerge pages first, then to 1 after changing merge_across_nodes, to remerge according to the new setting." Let's fix it by tracking in ksm_nr_node_ids the actual number of allocated tree roots. remove_all_stable_nodes() and ksm_check_stable_tree() will now scan more tree roots (skipping the empty ones), which is harmless.

items.title: CVE-2026-99652: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix deadlock of mremap() against UFFDIO_MOVE With per-VMA locks, UFFDIO_MOVE can run concurrently with mre
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix deadlock of mremap() against UFFDIO_MOVE With per-VMA locks, UFFDIO_MOVE can run concurrently with mremap() on different VMAs in the same mm. Those VMAs can share page tables, so both operations can acquire the same pair of page-table locks. UFFDIO_MOVE orders the locks by address, while mremap() takes the source lock first. These conflicting orders can deadlock; mremap() holding mmap_lock for writing no longer helps. Move double_pt_lock() and double_pt_unlock() to mm/internal.h and use them for all page-table moves in mremap(). Preserve the source entry checks after acquiring both locks. Remove the comments claiming that exclusive mmap_lock makes lock ordering irrelevant. In move_ptes(), make sure to just recheck source and destination PMD after taking the locks and drop the overly-long comment. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: use new helpers consistently; simplify description and comments; move_ptes() fixup ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99639: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fix whiteout creation in casefolded directories unlink and rmdir fail with EINVAL on an overlay with case
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fix whiteout creation in casefolded directories unlink and rmdir fail with EINVAL on an overlay with casefolded (case-insensitive) layers, if the name exists in a lower layer. With casefolded directories, both dentries can be unhashed: - The target. items.title: CVE-2026-99640: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: do not let chattr change the casefold flag chattr +F or -F on an overlay directory can make the directory
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: do not let chattr change the casefold flag chattr +F or -F on an overlay directory can make the directory, or the whole mount, unusable. Lookups of the directory, and lookups in it, then fail. From code inspection, the caller only needs to own the directory. items.title: CVE-2026-99641: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fail the mount if the casefold flag has changed An unprivileged user in a user namespace can repeatedly t
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fail the mount if the casefold flag has changed An unprivileged user in a user namespace can repeatedly trigger a kernel warning with their own overlay mounts. They do so by changing the casefold flag of the topmost layer's empty root, the top directory of that layer, after the layers are set and before the mount is created. The casefold flag of a directory makes name lookups in that directory case-insensitive. All layers of an overlay must agree on casefolding. ovl_mount_dir_check() reads the casefold flag of a layer root when fsconfig() sets that layer, and saves the result in ofs->casefold. The mount is created later, by another fsconfig() call with FSCONFIG_CMD_CREATE. The casefold flag of an empty directory can be changed. The casefold flag of the overlay root must match ofs->casefold. ovl_get_root() copies the flag from the topmost layer root, as it is when the mount is created. On a mismatch, ovl_get_root() only does a WARN_ON(), and the mount continues. The check is not a WARN_ON_ONCE(), so each such mount warns again. An unprivileged user needs CONFIG_UNICODE, and a tmpfs mounted with the casefold opt

items.title: CVE-2026-99642: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check folio->mapping under folio lock in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios from the pa
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check folio->mapping under folio lock in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios from the page cache without taking the folio lock. khugepaged or MADV_COLLAPSE can therefore replace a folio after checking its refcount while memfd_pin_folios() still pins the old folio. The caller then receives a folio which is no longer part of the memfd. For udmabuf and iommufd, this can cause data corruption: DMA accesses the detached folio rather than the live memfd contents. DMA reads can return stale data, while DMA writes update the detached copy and are lost from the live memfd. The detached folio remains pinned, so these accesses do not constitute a use-after-free or target another application's memory. For memfd live update, the stale contents can reappear in the memfd after handover. Lock the folio and recheck folio->mapping before pinning it, like other page cache users do. If the folio was removed, retry the folio lookup from the index that was removed.

items.title: CVE-2026-99643: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: khugepaged: fix readahead lock inversion in collapse_file() collapse_file() can call page_cache_sync_readahead
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: khugepaged: fix readahead lock inversion in collapse_file() collapse_file() can call page_cache_sync_readahead() while still holding source folios locked. If truncate holds mapping->invalidate_lock exclusively and waits for one of those folios, readahead waits for invalidate_lock and neither side can make progress. We need to release those folio locks before starting readahead. On a page cache miss, roll back first, populate the collapse range, and retry once. Doing readahead after rollback avoids an extra pass when all folios are already present. If another miss occurs on retry, give up rather than keep retrying while truncate or reclaim removes folios. Keep page_cache_sync_readahead() and wait for read I/O with filemap_lock_folio(), releasing each folio before moving to the next. The existing uptodate check during collapse still handles read errors. Shmem uses shmem_get_folio() for swapin and fallocated folios without taking mapping->invalidate_lock, so it is unaffected.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory-tiers: unregister empty tiers outside memory_tier_lock When offlining a node's last memory empties its tier, clear_node_memory_tier() calls device_unregister() while holding memory_tier_lock. A concurrent sysfs read can hold a kernfs active reference and block in nodelist_show() on that mutex. device_unregister() then waits in kernfs_drain() for the read to finish and release its active reference, while the reader waits for the offlining task to release the mutex. Return the node's former tier from clear_node_memory_tier(), making the helper more similar to set_node_memory_tier(), which also returns a memory_tier pointer. Let the caller unlink an empty tier under memory_tier_lock before rebuilding demotion targets, then unregister its device after dropping the lock.

items.title: CVE-2026-99630: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e. one w
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e. one which doesn't share the root reservation, goes to the individual needs_update list when it is evicted. The user queue restore looked at vm->invalidated for them, which the VM state machine rework turned into the always_valid evicted list and commit 18decfc9e8cc ("drm/amdgpu/userq: actually validate userq BOs") into the individual evicted one. That list only holds imported DMA-bufs of compute VMs though, so for a user queue VM nothing is validated. The restore then neither locks such a BO nor moves it back. Its PTEs are updated to wherever it is now, cleared if it went to system memory, and it doesn't get the new eviction fence, so it can move again under the running queue. On navi48, once the BOs of an SDMA user queue are evicted from GTT (debugfs amdgpu_evict_gtt) the queue faults on its ring and rptr: amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: in page starting at address 0x0000000100000000 from client 10 amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA0 (0xd) amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: in page starting at address 0x0000000100101000

items.title: CVE-2026-99631: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: check amdgpu_vm_ready() in dma-buf move notify amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify() touches the page table
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: check amdgpu_vm_ready() in dma-buf move notify amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify() touches the page tables without first calling amdgpu_vm_ready(). When a process is SIGKILLed, its VM entities are stopped. Teardown of an imported dma-buf then tries to clear PTEs by submitting to one of those stopped entities. That eventually hangs the task. Commit aa5fc4362fac ("drm/amdgpu: fix task hang from failed job submission during process kill") added the stopped entity check in amdgpu_vm_ready() and used it in amdgpu_cs_vm_handling(). That did not cover a call in amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify(), what was already mentioned in: https://lists.freedesktop.org/archives/amd-gfx/2025-October/133076.html Tested by SIGKILLing a GPU workload holding imported dma-bufs. Without the patch "Trying to push to a killed entity" errors are logged, then a task hangs. With the patch there are no hung tasks. This was tested on a 6.18 kernel. (cherry picked from commit bee5c9d7a34cb1b510ad3b4c18c30f9d38b0ab7d)

items.title: CVE-2026-99634: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to sub
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to subflow_syn_recv_sock(). For an MP_JOIN request this takes the fatal fallback: the cloned child is destroyed and handed back with drop_req flagged, but tcp_fastopen_create_child() does not check the flag and queues it, so accept() can expose the freed child. MP_JOIN cannot use Fast Open: data on a subflow requires the completed HMAC exchange (RFC 8684, sec. 3.2). Refuse it (only the TFO path passes a SYN skb here) and let tcp_conn_request() fall back to the regular MP_JOIN handshake; also strip the Fast Open cookie from MP_JOIN SYN/ACKs. [ Moving code to avoid clearing TS and consolidating checks. ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99635: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost/vsock: size receive SKBs from declared payload vhost_vsock_alloc_skb() sizes the skb from iov_length(),
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost/vsock: size receive SKBs from declared payload vhost_vsock_alloc_skb() sizes the skb from iov_length(), the total guest descriptor length. virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt() instead adds hdr->len to rx_bytes and buf_used, and budgets each queued skb as SKB_TRUESIZE(0). The guest controls the descriptor length and hdr->len independently. A guest can therefore provide a 64 KiB descriptor while declaring a zero payload. The descriptor-sized skb remains queued, rx_bytes and buf_used remain unchanged, and only the fixed queue-entry budget limits retention. This is not a lifetime leak: the skb is freed when dequeued or at socket teardown. Repeating this across connections can nevertheless exhaust host memory. On Linux v7.2, 455 such descriptors retained 30,255,680 bytes for a 262,144-byte receive buffer; a full-payload control retained 265,984 bytes. Vhost previously read hdr->len and allocated pkt->buf from that value. The conversion from virtio_vsock_pkt to sk_buff instead allocated receive skbs from the descriptor length, introducing the allocation-accounting mismatch. Copy the header into a stack object and validate

items.title: CVE-2026-99636: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: reject a negative TCP header offset in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() stores skb_tra
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: reject a negative TCP header offset in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() stores skb_transport_offset(), or the inner offset, in the unsigned hdr_len. A header in front of skb->data gives a negative offset. For an offset a little below zero, pskb_may_pull() gets a small length and succeeds. Then a 64-bit kernel reads the TCP header far after the skb and can crash. Further below zero pskb_may_pull() fails. Commit 28a57fb2c5df ("net: iptunnel: fix stale transport header during tunnel decapsulation") fixed one source of such offsets. Other code that removes bytes from the front of a packet can leave the same stale header. Return SKB_DROP_REASON_SKB_BAD_GSO for a negative offset in the TCP branch. SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 and the other GSO types read no header and still get a wrong qdisc_pkt_len(). On a 64-bit kernel only packets that cause the read after the skb today get a new result. Then __dev_queue_xmit() drops them and returns -EINVAL, but sch_handle_ingress() ignores the result. Their content can be valid. Thus the code that leaves the header stale needs its own fix.

items.title: CVE-2026-99637: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: inherit FMODE_NONOTIFY when opening directory realfiles When fanotify hands a listener an fd for a permis
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: inherit FMODE_NONOTIFY when opening directory realfiles When fanotify hands a listener an fd for a permission event on an overlay directory, ovl_dir_open_realfile() opens the real directory via dentry_open(), not backing_file_open(), so the lower open could still raise FS_OPEN_PERM and deadlock a listener that also marks the backing filesystem. Export dentry_open_nonotify() and call it from ovl_path_open_realfile() when the overlay user file must not generate events. Ordinary ovl_path_open() callers are unchanged.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amd/display: Fix NULL deref in dcn401_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto [Why] resource_get_otg_master_for_stream() can return NULL if no OTG master pipe is found for a given stream. items.title: CVE-2026-99627: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu/gfx12: disallow GFXOFF while updating the SPM VMID gfx_v12_0_update_spm_vmid() does a read-modify-w
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu/gfx12: disallow GFXOFF while updating the SPM VMID gfx_v12_0_update_spm_vmid() does a read-modify-write of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL over MMIO without keeping GFX powered, unlike gfx11. On navi48, after a few other submissions and a VM fault on the same VM, a COPY_DATA of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL from such a job reads 0 although the update was called for it: $ amd_uapi_regression --run-subtest cs-secure-ib-compute,gem-mapping-info-high-va,gpuvm-fault-high-va,reserved-vmid-spm-vmid amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: [gfxhub] page fault (src_id:0 ring:40 vmid:7 pasid:185) amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA1 (0xe) RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL in the job: 0x00000000 With GFXOFF disallowed around the update it reads the reserved VMID 15. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amd/display: Avoid closing unowned DDC pins [WHY] dal_ddc_open() cleans up pins it acquires on later failures. If the data-pin open fails, this attempt acquired nothing. If opening the clock pin or configuring fails, dal_ddc_open() closes the pins it opened. An extra dal_ddc_close() is unnecessary and unsafe: GPIO_RESULT_ALREADY_OPENED can mean AUX owns the existing handles, and closing them here would disrupt AUX. items.title: CVE-2026-99616: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: look up the index by the decoded origin A file opened by file handle on an overlay with nfs_export=on can
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: look up the index by the decoded origin A file opened by file handle on an overlay with nfs_export=on can show the stale lower data of a file that was copied up to the upper layer. While the file opened this way stays in the inode cache, a lookup of the copied up file by path fails with ESTALE for all users. The open can also succeed for a file that was removed, where it has to fail with ESTALE. This happens with a handle that has one byte changed. The handle comes from an NFS client, or from a process that calls open_by_handle_at() with CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH in the initial user namespace. When a file in a lower layer is about to be modified, overlayfs first copies it to the upper layer (copy up). With nfs_export=on, each copy up also creates an entry in the index directory, a directory that overlayfs keeps for itself on the upper filesystem. The handle of an overlay file that comes from a lower layer wraps the handle of its lower inode. Overlayfs calls this lower inode the origin. The overlay handle stays valid after a copy up. items.title: CVE-2026-99617: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: arm64: mm: validate /dev/mem mmap ranges without overflow An arm64 syzkaller reproducer creates a FUSE charact
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: arm64: mm: validate /dev/mem mmap ranges without overflow An arm64 syzkaller reproducer creates a FUSE character device with major:minor 1:1, so opening it uses the /dev/mem file operations. It maps one page from offset 0xfffffffffffff000 at user address zero. The next openat() with a NULL pathname triggers a synchronous external abort (SEA, ESR 0x96000010) in strncpy_from_user() via do_getname(), panicking the kernel. valid_mmap_phys_addr_range() checks the exclusive end by adding the mapping size to the starting address. For this offset, the sum wraps to zero and passes the PHYS_MASK test, allowing an out-of-range PFN to reach remap_pfn_range(). The inclusive-end overflow check in mmap_mem_prepare() does not catch it because the end is ULONG_MAX. Reject starting PFNs outside PHYS_MASK and compare the inclusive length against the remaining physical range without overflowing. This also allows mappings that end exactly at PHYS_MASK, which the old check incorrectly rejects. [catalin.marinas@arm.com: changed the check to look more like __access_ok()]

items.title: CVE-2026-99618: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: don't return memory contents beyond valid data when reading ANA log page The host side does not know ho
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: don't return memory contents beyond valid data when reading ANA log page The host side does not know how much valid data will be returned by the target so it will typically provide a buffer larger than the amount of valid data in the ANA log page. The memory allocation used by the target does not guarantee that prior kernel memory contents will not be returned past the end of the valid page data. Fix this to ensure that the SGL is zeroed before copying the data.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: unlock the VM and BO when attaching a KFD BO fails kfd_mem_attach() locks the page directory and the BO with a drm_exec transaction on its stack, but leaves through the unwind label without drm_exec_fini() when locking fails, e.g. when MAP_MEMORY_TO_GPU gets a signal while the page directory or the BO is busy. With one thread doing GEM_VA map/unmap on the KFD VM and another one mapping KFD BOs while getting SIGUSR1 every 20 us: BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in __ww_mutex_lock.constprop.0+0x34f5/0x3da0 ww_mutex_lock_interruptible+0x2f/0x150 drm_exec_lock_obj+0x107/0x2d0 [drm_exec] kfd_mem_attach+0x4dd/0x1b60 [amdgpu] and the process ends up in D state. items.title: CVE-2026-99622: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: drop the dma-buf reference when a KFD import fails import_obj_create() takes a reference on the dm
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: drop the dma-buf reference when a KFD import fails import_obj_create() takes a reference on the dma-buf for the new kgd_mem, but the error path after validating the BO doesn't drop it. Since the validation reserves the BO interruptibly, an import failing with -ERESTARTSYS leaks the exported BO with its memory, and keeps the module in use. Importing a 64 MiB VRAM BO in a loop while getting SIGUSR1 every 20 us and another thread changes the BO's mappings: INFO: 171821 imports, VRAM used before 65 MiB, after 129 MiB modprobe: FATAL: Module amdgpu is in use. Drop the reference, and free the sync object and the mutex of the kgd_mem as well. With that VRAM usage returns to 65 MiB after the same test. (cherry picked from commit b4d1eca2729840148ff2ea957724ce764ca5a94e)

items.title: CVE-2026-99609: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Require a buffer of two URBs usx2y_urb_capt_retire() wraps the ring buffer once per packet and us
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Require a buffer of two URBs usx2y_urb_capt_retire() wraps the ring buffer once per packet and usx2y_urb_play_prepare() once per URB of nr_of_packs() packets of up to 50 frames. Both assume that the data fits in the buffer, and the hw constraints only require about two 1 ms periods, so a packet larger than the buffer on capture, or a URB larger than the buffer on playback, violates that assumption. Constrain SNDRV_PCM_HW_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE in snd_usx2y_pcm_open() to at least two URBs, 2 * nr_of_packs() * 50 frames, for both directions. The bound is in frames and derived from the driver's own packet limit, so it does not read the endpoint, whose altsetting is only selected in prepare. Two URBs rather than one, because the position advances by a URB on playback and only moves when a URB is less than the whole buffer. Keep a guard in usx2y_urb_capt_retire() that drops a packet larger than the buffer, for the case the constraint makes unreachable. items.title: CVE-2026-99610: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: caiaq: free the EP4 URB when input setup fails The three controllers that use the EP4 input URB allocate
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: caiaq: free the EP4 URB when input setup fails The three controllers that use the EP4 input URB allocate it before checking the endpoint type and before registering the input device. On failure they jump to exit_free_idev, which clears cdev->input_dev but leaves cdev->ep4_in_urb set. The card teardown then calls snd_usb_caiaq_input_free(), which returns early because input_dev is NULL, so the URB is never freed. Release the URB before dropping the input device on the error path.

items.title: CVE-2026-99611: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: line6: Reject capture buffers smaller than two packets line6_capture_copy() splits the copy into the ALS

The packet size comes from the device's endpoint, and the per-device hw structs allow 64-byte periods with periods_min 1, so a packet can be larger than the whole buffer. audio_in_callback() logs an oversized packet and then copies it anyway. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: hda/tas2781: Only accept CRC-less V1 data if all entries are valid Commit 408249089c48 ("ALSA: hda/tas2781: Accept V1 calibration data without CRC") only checked the first device entry. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: l2tp: only return sessions of the given tunnel in l2tp_session_get() Commit 5f77c18ea556 ("l2tp: use IDR for all session lookups") made pppol2tp_connect() and the netlink session commands find sessions with l2tp_session_get(), passing the socket of the tunnel they name. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: check the unallocated space table when it is loaded udf_table_new_block() hands out the first block of the extent closest to its goal and trusts that the extent covers at least one whole block inside the partition. Nothing checks that. A zero-length extent makes it return the block the extent points at, which need not be free, and the subtraction of one block then underflows the length into the type bits, turning the entry into a bogus continuation. An extent running past the end of the partition makes it return blocks behind the partition. Such tables are not only found on crafted images: until the previous commit, udf_table_new_block() itself left zero-length extents behind in tables written by mkudffs, and then converted them into extents running past the partition. Check every extent once when the table is loaded, and refuse read-write access if one is empty, is not a whole number of blocks, or does not lie inside the partition, in the same way as for other allocation information the kernel cannot use. items.title: CVE-2026-99602: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: don't let the extent type hide an exhausted free-space table extent udf_table_new_block() takes the first
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: don't let the extent type hide an exhausted free-space table extent udf_table_new_block() takes the first block of the free-space table extent closest to the goal. It keeps that extent's type and length together in goal_elen, subtracts one block, and deletes the extent only if goal_elen then reaches zero. UDF 2.60 section 2.3.7.1 requires the free-space extents of an Unallocated Space Entry to be of type 1 (allocated but not recorded), and mkudffs writes them that way. For such an extent the type bits keep goal_elen non-zero, so taking its last block leaves a type-1 extent of length zero behind, starting at the block after the extent, which is in use. The next allocation that picks this empty extent returns that in-use block. Subtracting a block from 0x40000000 then borrows from the type bits, and the extent becomes type 0 with a length of 2^30 - blocksize: about a gigabyte of "free" space overlapping live metadata, the other table extents and whatever lies behind the partition. items.title: CVE-2026-99603: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: pm: kernel: use RCU to free endpoint listeners mptcp_pm_nl_create_listen_socket() starts the TCP listen
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: pm: kernel: use RCU to free endpoint listeners mptcp_pm_nl_create_listen_socket() starts the TCP listener directly instead of going through mptcp_listen(). It consequently misses setting SOCK_RCU_FREE on the parent MPTCP socket. tcp_child_process() can invoke the listener's subflow_data_ready() callback without holding the MPTCP parent lock or a reference to the parent. An authenticated MP_JOIN racing with endpoint teardown can therefore access the parent after its last reference has been dropped. The ADD_ADDR error path can also close an already published listener. Set SOCK_RCU_FREE before __inet_listen_sk() publishes the TCP listener, matching mptcp_listen(). This protects the parent on every subsequent close path, including a failed endpoint addition.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/etnaviv: Flush the tile status cache through both the PE and BLT Since commit f232d9ec029c ("drm/etnaviv: fix TS cache flushing on GPUs with BLT engine"), jobs on GPUs with a BLT engine use a BLT command to flush the tile status cache instead of TS_FLUSH_CACHE, which is broken on most of these GPUs. GC7000 r6008/r6009 and GC8200 r6401 are the other way around: TS_FLUSH_CACHE works, but the BLT command does not flush the cache. The vendor driver handles these GPUs using TS_FLUSH_CACHE, but the etnaviv kernel driver has no way to identify them. As a result, dirty tile status cache lines survive the end of a job. They are written back by the next cache flush, using the page table of the job issuing it. If that job belongs to another process, the write goes to the wrong address space. On GC7000 r6009 this causes MMU faults and GPU recoveries blamed on an innocent process. I see around 1100 per run of a multisample depth/stencil test running alongside two other GPU clients. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/etnaviv: Fix NULL dereference on unbind without PPU flop reset flop_reset_data_ppu is only allocated on GPUs that need the PPU flop reset. However, etnaviv_unbind(..) frees it unconditionally, and etnaviv_cmdbuf_free(..) dereferences cmdbuf->suballoc before checking whether cmdbuf is NULL. As a result, unloading the driver on GPUs that do not need the PPU flop reset causes a NULL pointer dereference at address 0.

items.title: CVE-2026-99606: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/smc: don't spin in smc_rx_recvmsg() while a pipe holds spliced data While bytes spliced off the RMB are st
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/smc: don't spin in smc_rx_recvmsg() while a pipe holds spliced data While bytes spliced off the RMB are still in a pipe, recvmsg() waits for the pipe to release them before it copies the data behind them. The path to that wait skips the timeout and signal checks, and smc_rx_wait() returns at once on RCV_SHUTDOWN. With a signal pending, after SHUT_RD, or once the peer closes or shuts down writing, recvmsg() spins on a CPU until the pipe is drained, and SIGKILL cannot stop it. MSG_DONTWAIT and an expired SO_RCVTIMEO wait there too instead of returning -EAGAIN. Check the timeout and signals before that wait, and end it when the pipe releases the data or the connection is killed, not on RCV_SHUTDOWN. A zero-length read returns 0 without waiting for the pipe; a non-blocking one returns -EAGAIN while poll() still reports the socket readable (splice() can still take those bytes). The wait sets SOCKWQ_ASYNC_WAITDATA like smc_rx_wait(), so a byte arriving behind the pipe raises no SIGIO on a reader already asleep for it, and a full barrier orders its wait queue entry before its read of splice_pending, so no wake is lost

items.title: CVE-2026-99607: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ext2: preserve IOMAP_F_DIRTY for extending direct writes ext2_iomap_begin() sets IOMAP_F_DIRTY for writes that
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ext2: preserve IOMAP_F_DIRTY for extending direct writes ext2_iomap_begin() sets IOMAP_F_DIRTY for writes that may extend i_size, but clears the flag after ext2_get_blocks(). When the write uses an existing mapped block, iomap can then use FUA and skip generic_write_sync(), even though ext2_dio_write_end_io() updates the inode size. An O_DSYNC write can therefore return without persisting the new size. For example, on a FUA-capable device, a 512-byte O_DIRECT|O_DSYNC write at offset 512 into a fsynced one-byte file returns successfully and extends the in-memory size to 1024, while an immediate read of the on-disk inode still shows size 1. An explicit fsync persists the new size. Move setting of IOMAP_F_DIRTY after the initialization.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Guard the playback copy usx2y_urb_play_prepare() sums the packet lengths of a whole URB, copies that many frames with a single wrap, and sizes each playback packet from the capture packet's actual_length. Three things are unchecked: that the URB fits in the ring buffer, that a packet fits in the playback endpoint's maxpacksize, from which tmpbuf is allocated, and that actual_length is a whole number of frames. The ISO descriptors take the raw actual_length while transfer_buffer_length and the copies take count * stride, so a packet that is not a multiple of the stride makes the descriptors add up to more than the buffer, by up to stride - 1 bytes per packet. Return -EPIPE, as the existing packet-size check does, when the URB is larger than the buffer or a packet is larger than maxpacksize, and size each descriptor from whole frames, so the descriptors add up to transfer_buffer_length and each stays within maxpacksize. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sched/fair: Clear throttle state when leaving the fair class Task-based CFS bandwidth throttling removes a task's fair sched_entity while the scheduler core still considers the task queued. p->throttled carries the fair-specific state across dequeue/enqueue operations. DEQUEUE_CLASS removes the task from cfs_rq->throttled_limbo_list but retains the bit. If the last finite CFS quota is disabled while the task runs in another class, it is absent from the unthrottle walk and the bit survives. Returning to fair while cfs_bandwidth_used() is false then performs a real fair enqueue with p->throttled still set. After bandwidth is re-enabled, a class-change dequeue treats the stale bit as limbo state and skips __dequeue_task(). p->se.on_rq therefore remains set, and put_prev_task_fair() places the entity in the EEVDF tree while the task moves to RT. On exit, the fair picker can select the TASK_DEAD task. __schedule() then returns to do_task_dead(), which hits BUG(). items.title: CVE-2026-99597: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: srcu: Add list_splice_init_srcu() list_splice_init_rcu() makes a list look empty to new readers, waits for the
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: srcu: Add list_splice_init_srcu() list_splice_init_rcu() makes a list look empty to new readers, waits for the current ones with the given sync function, and only then links the entries into the new list. The sync function takes no argument, so it can wait for RCU readers but not for the readers of an srcu_struct. Passing synchronize_rcu() for a list read under SRCU still builds, but leaves SRCU readers on the entries while the last one's next pointer is moved onto the new list head. nvme_remove_namespaces() does this today. Add list_splice_init_srcu(), which waits for the readers of the given srcu_struct instead.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: MIPS: sgi-ip32: Leave MACE PCI control alone in config accesses mace_pci_read_config() clears the master abort interrupt enable in the MACE PCI control register around each config read. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: don't use eloc after the end of the unallocated space table When udf_next_aext() returns 0, its eloc, elen and etype outputs hold no defined value. Only take the extent if the walk stopped at it. items.title: CVE-2026-99600: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: fix preallocation discarding before an empty allocation extent udf_discard_prealloc() finds the last exte
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: fix preallocation discarding before an empty allocation extent udf_discard_prealloc() finds the last extent of a file by peeking at the next one with udf_next_aext() and stopping when that returns 0. The peek reads into eloc and elen, and the code then uses them as the last extent. But when udf_next_aext() returns 0 they hold no defined value: if the extent list ends in a continuation descriptor that leads to an empty allocation extent, they describe that continuation, i.e. the block of the empty allocation extent, one block long. The kernel creates such lists itself: when udf_delete_aext() removes the only descriptor of the last allocation extent in a list, it leaves that allocation extent empty and the continuation to it in place. If the last extent is a preallocation, udf_discard_prealloc() deletes it with udf_delete_aext(), which finds the following allocation extent empty, so it also removes the continuation and frees that allocation extent's block. udf_discard_prealloc() then frees eloc and elen: that block a second time, instead of the preallocated blocks. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommu/arm-smmu-v3: Handle ARM erratum for CONT under invalidation with SVA The erratum (MMU-700: #3777127, S3: #3673557) deals with under invalidation of a CONT PTE grouping in the SMMU. The recommended work around is to use a range invalidation that spans the entire CONT. The only user of CONT in the kernel right now is through SVA sharing a CPU page table that contains a CONT created by the mm. Previously it was thought that this errata was dealt with because the driver always uses range invalidation. However, there is a subtle detail in the errata that the invalidation range must fully enclose the entire CONT for it to work. It seems that two sequential range invalidations, with a split point falling inside a CONT grouping, will not prevent the errata. The SMMU's range invalidation generation algorithm does not produce a single invalidation for a single SVA invalidation request, nor does the mm carefully align the SVA invalidation ranges to accommodate the splitting of the invalidation into several ranges. items.title: CVE-2026-99587: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ata: libata-scsi: reject data-in commands with a data-out buffer SG_IO can submit a data-in SCSI command with
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ata: libata-scsi: reject data-in commands with a data-out buffer SG_IO can submit a data-in SCSI command with DMA_TO_DEVICE. The scatterlist can then contain pages pinned without write access. ata_scsi_rbuf_fill() writes simulated replies to that scatterlist; in the reported case, the copy tried to write the shared zero page and faulted in the kernel. The same mismatch can affect SG_IO commands translated by libata. ZBC IN and GET PHYSICAL ELEMENT STATUS completion handlers can modify the receive buffer even if the drive aborts the command. For ATAPI, the successful INQUIRY completion also rewrites the buffer in atapi_fixup_inquiry(). Reject these mismatched commands before the buffer is written or the command is issued. Report ABORTED COMMAND / DATA IN BUFFER ERROR because the CDB itself can be valid; the supplied transfer direction is wrong.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: batman-adv: tt: only update flags for TT events In the first implementation of the translation table events, it was only possible to announce: * ADD: new locally detected client * DEL: disappeared local client If an ADD event was queued and then a DEL event was queued in the same timeslot, it is valid to destroy both events because nothing actually changed for remode nodes But with commit 3c4f7ab60cc2 ("batman-adv: improve the TT component to support runtime flag changes") and subsequent changes, it could also happen that there are extra ADD events: * ADD: _NEW_ locally detected client * ADD: already existing client with new flags * DEL: disappeared local client The first and the last type of event could in theory still be removed together from the (to be announced) events queue. But if the "update flags" ADD is dropped together with the DEL, it would still leave global translation table of a remote node in the incorrect state - believing that the client didn't disappear. items.title: CVE-2026-99589: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: batman-adv: tt: clear ROAM flag when re-adding a pending local client When a ROAMING_ADV is received for an an
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: batman-adv: tt: clear ROAM flag when re-adding a pending local client When a ROAMING_ADV is received for an announced local client, batadv_tt_local_mark_removed() sets BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM, queues a DEL|ROAM change and marks the entry as BATADV_TT_CLIENT_PENDING. If the client sends a frame again before the next TTVN commit, batadv_tt_local_add_existing() only clears the PENDING flag and returns early. The ADD cancels the queued DEL, but the entry keeps the ROAM flag: * batadv_is_my_client() reports the client as not served by this node * batadv_tt_local_client_is_roaming() reroutes unicast frames for it to the node which sent the ROAMING_ADV The ROAM flag is only removed with the next frame of the client. Since BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM is set together with BATADV_TT_CLIENT_PENDING, it has to be cleared also at the same time with BATADV_TT_CLIENT_PENDING when the client roamed back.

items.title: CVE-2026-99590: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: clamp the inline data length in ceph_fill_inline_data() The MDS decides how much inline data to attach t
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: clamp the inline data length in ceph_fill_inline_data() The MDS decides how much inline data to attach to a reply, and the client parses inline_len without any upper bound: ceph_decode_need() only verifies that the message actually carries that many bytes. ceph_fill_inline_data() then copies the data into a single folio with no length check, so a malicious or buggy MDS returning more inline data than the folio can hold writes past its end. Clamp the length to folio_size() so both callers, handle_cap_grant() and fill_inode(), are covered.

items.title: CVE-2026-99591: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommu/amd: Force device table to maximum size IOMMU can perform out-of-bounds read of the device table entry (
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommu/amd: Force device table to maximum size IOMMU can perform out-of-bounds read of the device table entry (DTE) that is adjacent to the last DTE and falls outside the device table. For example, if the device table can hold 0 to N-1 entries, then the IOMMU can be made to fetch the Nth entry, which falls outside the device table. The device table is owned by the hypervisor (HV) and is assigned in 4KB pages that are contiguous in system physical address (SPA). If the out-of-bound DTE falls on a guest-owned page, then the guest can exploit this bug to setup malicious table walks to corrupt HV pages and/or bring down the system. Note that this bug does not manifest when the device table size is set to its maximum size of 2MB. Therefore, force the device table size to the maximum 2MB on affected processors. These are CPU family 0x17 (Zen1/Zen2) through family 0x1a (Zen5/BRH). items.title: CVE-2026-99592: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: x86/mm: Fix global ASID handed out to two processes On AMD CPUs with INVLPGB, two live processes can get the s
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: x86/mm: Fix global ASID handed out to two processes On AMD CPUs with INVLPGB, two live processes can get the same MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE global ASID value. The two then hit each other's TLB entries, so each can read or corrupt the other's memory. The global ASID space is managed lazily. When a global ASID is freed, its bit is set in the global_asid_freed bitmap. Once the free ASID search reaches the end of the global_asid_used bitmap, a global flush is done to really reclaim the lazily freed global ASIDs. However, the current code can assign the same global ASID to two different processes, if one process is assigned MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE - 1, another process MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE, and both stick around (keeping their global ASID numbers in use) until the search wraps around again. At that point a third process could also get assigned MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE. the highest ASID stays in use, so it is not handed out again last_global_asid stays below it, so no reset the clear bits run out find_next_zero_bit() returns MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE global_asid_available > 0, so the failure is not caught MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE is handed out as an ASID

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: arm64: sdei: Preserve the interrupted context's exception registers An SDEI event is dispatched by firmware regardless of PSTATE.DAIF, so it can interrupt the kernel where the exception registers are live: - exception entry, before kernel_entry has saved ELR_EL1/SPSR_EL1 and before the C handler has read ESR_EL1/FAR_EL1; - exception return, after kernel_exit has loaded ELR_EL1/SPSR_EL1 and before the ERET. An IRQ or pseudo-NMI cannot arrive there with PSTATE.I set. Firmware saves only x0-x17, PC and PSTATE around an SDEI event, so a synchronous exception taken by the handler overwrites the interrupted context's ELR, SPSR, ESR and FAR. do_sdei_event() only notices that ELR changed, and warns. The interrupted context then carries on with the handler's state. A task interrupted on its way into the kernel can be sent SIGILL for the handler's kernel data abort. A task interrupted on its way back to user space ERETs to EL1, at the handler's fixup address, with user registers loaded. With SDEI delivering NMI backtraces, this happens in normal operation. items.title: CVE-2026-99579: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: honour F_SEAL_EXEC when an ACL is set The owner of a memfd sealed with F_SEAL_EXEC can still change
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: honour F_SEAL_EXEC when an ACL is set The owner of a memfd sealed with F_SEAL_EXEC can still change its execute bits by setting a POSIX access ACL. With CONFIG_TMPFS_POSIX_ACL, this lets an unprivileged owner make a non-executable memfd executable, bypassing vm.memfd_noexec=2. simple_set_acl() updates i_mode directly, bypassing the seal check in shmem_setattr(). Add shmem_set_acl() to check the resulting mode. Share the F_SEAL_EXEC check with shmem_setattr() using memfd_check_seals_mode() in include/linux/memfd.h. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: use common helper; simplify description ]

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/userfaultfd: only allocate anon_vma in CoW mappings find_vma_and_prepare_anon() can end up allocating an anon_vma in VMAs that are not CoW mappings, which is wrong. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: platform/chrome: cros_usbpd_notify: Only use drvdata when parent is GOOG0004 cros_usbpd_notify_probe_acpi() takes the EC device pointer from dev_get_drvdata(dev->parent) and assumes it is a struct cros_ec_device. items.title: CVE-2026-99582: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sctp: re-point retained control chunks on association migration sctp_sock_migrate() transfers DATA chunk owner
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sctp: re-point retained control chunks on association migration sctp_sock_migrate() transfers DATA chunk ownership but leaves retained control chunks pointing at the old socket. A later retransmission can therefore access the socket after it has been freed. Extend the migration walk to cover retained control chunks and use sctp_control_set_owner_w() to assign their new owner. Reuse the DATA ownership check so each chunk is processed once per pass, even when it is reachable through multiple lists or retained pointers. Preserve a control chunk's existing authentication key across migration so its final release can still generate SCTP_AUTH_FREE_KEY when needed.

items.title: CVE-2026-99583: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sctp: hold shkey across socket migration sctp_sock_migrate() transfers queued DATA skbs from the old socket to
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sctp: hold shkey across socket migration sctp_sock_migrate() transfers queued DATA skbs from the old socket to the new one. skb_orphan() invokes sctp_wfree() during that transfer and drops the skb-owned shared-key reference. If userspace has removed that key from the association, this can be the final reference. The following sctp_set_owner_w() then dereferences the freed chunk->shkey while trying to take the new owner reference. Take a temporary shared-key reference before orphaning the skb and release it after the new owner has taken its reference. This preserves the selected authentication key throughout the ownership transfer. Bug found and triaged by OpenAI Security Research and validated by Trail of Bits.

items.title: CVE-2026-99585: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: arm64: Use kvm_s2_fault_vma_info in gmem_abort() gmem_abort() maps at s2fd->fault_ipa, which HPFAR_EL2 ho
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: arm64: Use kvm_s2_fault_vma_info in gmem_abort() gmem_abort() maps at s2fd->fault_ipa, which HPFAR_EL2 holds at 4K granularity whatever the page size. The generic page-table code aligns it, but pkvm_pgtable_stage2_map() looks up existing mappings over [addr, addr + size), so on a pKVM host with pages larger than 4K a guest_memfd-backed guest that faults past the first 4K of a page can find its neighbour's mapping, get -EAGAIN and take the same fault forever. The memory fault exit reports s2fd->fault_ipa too, which for a nested guest's fault is the nested IPA rather than the canonical one kvm_gmem_get_pfn() failed on. Take the addresses from kvm_s2_fault_vma_info instead, as user_mem_abort() does, and report the canonical gfn in the memory fault exit. kvm_s2_fault_get_vma_info() itself isn't called: a guest_memfd memslot's userspace_addr doesn't need to be backed by a VMA.

Check the queue liveness inside the queue lock, and clear queue->sock under the same lock. items.title: CVE-2026-99574: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: f2fs: bound the SIT/NAT bitmaps by the checkpoint pack sit_ver_bitmap_bytesize and nat_ver_bitmap_bytesize are
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: f2fs: bound the SIT/NAT bitmaps by the checkpoint pack sit_ver_bitmap_bytesize and nat_ver_bitmap_bytesize are used as memcpy lengths into and out of sbi->ckpt, which is sized from cp_payload alone, and nothing compares either length against that allocation. sanity_check_ckpt() has checked these two fields since c77ec61ca0a4, which added them after a crafted image overran build_sit_info(). That check ties each length to a segment count; it never compares either against the allocation, which is the half this adds. Mounting over-reads in build_sit_info() and build_node_manager(), and the first checkpoint writes the same lengths back through the same pointers, so the over-read's contents reach the on-disk checkpoint. An unmount is enough; the filesystem does not have to be used. Bound both ends the way __bitmap_ptr() lays them out. The three branches differ, so a single sum of the two lengths would still admit a small overflow when cp_payload is non-zero.

items.title: CVE-2026-99575: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: f2fs: return -EIO for a lost inode block after cp_error After cp_error, dirty node caches are dropped without
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: f2fs: return -EIO for a lost inode block after cp_error After cp_error, dirty node caches are dropped without being written. If such an inode was never written, its NAT entry is still NEW_ADDR, and reading its inode block returns -ENOENT. f2fs_get_dnode_of_data() passes that -ENOENT up, and callers take it as a hole. Since the inode block is missing, the next offset can only advance one block, so fiemap walks block by block up to maxbytes, about 2^30 blocks, while holding the inode lock. It took hours in a power-off recovery test after shutdown and blocked unlink and umount on the file. Return -EIO instead of -ENOENT when the inode block itself is missing after cp_error or shutdown. A missing direct or indirect node is still reported as -ENOENT.

This limit is set by the device driver/DMA controller (max_hw_sectors) and device-mapper targets. In f2fs, section_size strictly matches zone_size, and block allocation never spans across section boundaries, so bios never cross chunk_sectors. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: wifi: rtw88: usb: bound what the driver feeds the after-DTIM queue Frames routed to the high queue are transmitted right after DTIM beacons only, inside the ATIM window, while they wait in the shared TX page pool. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: wifi: rtw88: usb: route bmc frames via the high queue only for DTIM delivery In AP mode every broadcast and multicast data frame is routed to TX_DESC_QSEL_HIGH, the after-DTIM queue, whether or not anybody is asleep.
